note: Task-variation design study (workflow task-variation-design, 2026-10-10): capability designs, niche map, literature, engineering scout, headroom tests of hand-built positive controls, two critics, and the plan (docs/TASK_VARIATION_PLAN.md). Key scratch artifacts are copied next to this file; other paths are not kept.

findings.claim: In a fast, noisy SPECK world (d0 0.5, d_min 0.25, lam_bg 0.2) routing still pays after the reflex is re-tuned in that world. The re-tuned router leads by +2.31 ± 0.13. Lateral messages carry the lead, and the chains show multi-hop relay with hop-quantised latency. Routing passes A2 and A4 here.
findings.evidence: t11_retune.py, 512 fresh lives (block 13): re-tuning gave reflex@hollow3 +6.32 ± 0.09 (base knobs +4.99), reflex@ring3 +5.64 and router@ring4 +8.63 ± 0.12. Whole-life lateral_off on the router: dF -8.33 ± 0.12, 3.6 times the lead. t20 traces (2 lives): 58.4% of rim-motor spikes start in another column (reflex 0%), with latency 0.50 / 1.01 / 1.52 / 2.01 for 1-4 hops. Against base-tuned knobs (t1, 256 lives) the router's lead was +1.83 at base, +3.34 with fast conduction, +1.58 at 4x background and +2.17 with both. A smaller capture radius shrinks the lead (rho_c 0.7: +1.03; 0.5: +0.11), so it is dropped.

findings.claim: Re-tuning the reflex in each new world is essential. Without it, leads are overstated by about 1 F or more.
findings.evidence: In fast+noisy, re-tuning added +1.33 F to reflex@hollow3 and +1.13 to the router. In decoy-lite, the re-tuned reflex's centre sensor alone cut poison clicks from 38 to 16 per life (t15).

findings.claim: Wounds are the strongest new lever, and the existing kill_t / kill_frac keys already express them. A 25% kill at t=512 roughly halves the tuned reflex. Most of the loss comes from losing the hotspot (0,0,1) or the centre sensor (0,0,0), which no current body regrows.
findings.evidence: t3 and t7 (256 lives): reflex@hollow3 fell from 8.54 to 4.93. Captures after the wound fell from 10.2 to 2.3 per life, and 45% of lives had none. Lives where both K and C survived averaged 4.3 late captures; lives that lost C averaged 0.07 and lives that lost K 0.0. With kill_frac 0.5: 4.21. With the kill at t=300: 3.42.

findings.claim: A hand-built regenerating GRN body works as the positive control for regeneration. It refills holes, regrows the hotspot and centre, does not overgrow, and costs nothing when there is no wound.
findings.evidence: regen7.py: router_genome plus a slow INNER gene and four genes (GATE, MAT, FULL, LOSS), with K.w1 = 1. Against its non-regenerating twin: no wound -0.18 ± 0.14 (123 cells, unchanged); kill25@512 +2.17 ± 0.15; kill50@512 +1.27 ± 0.15; kill25@300 +3.22 ± 0.17. Against reflex@hollow3: +1.29, +0.86 and +1.73. t17 probes: 78% of killed sites refilled (router 9%, s5 24%); hotspot regrown in 63/63 lives (median 3.3 units) and centre in 71/71 (router 0/71). A division_off fork at the wound costs -2.47 ± 0.12. In a per-life family with half the lives wounded (t19, 512 lives): +0.96 ± 0.11 against its twin and +0.48 ± 0.14 against the reflex. It is -1.10 against the program-mode router, which does not pay for its own development.

findings.claim: Regeneration rules fail in instructive ways. A slow memory of the contact count is inherited by daughters and drives outward regrowth cascades. A memoryless 'exactly 6 contacts' rule fills every notch and so changes development. Lineage-defined roles cannot come back.
findings.evidence: regen.py to regen6.py: after a wound the body overgrew to 207-326 cells (from 96), or grew to 134-171 cells with no wound. F fell to 3.4-4.4 when the notch rule turned rim sensors into J relays. What worked: trigger only in mature cells that were interior, only after a lineage-timer gate. The centre's founder role cannot be regrown, so the hotspot must also accept a channel-1 (J-type) centre.

findings.claim: Evolved bodies do not regenerate usefully, so a wound world gives selection a genuinely new job. Their contact-count growth brake does not deliver regeneration for free.
findings.evidence: t17, s5 under kill25@512: 24% of killed sites refilled; hotspot regrown in 2/63 lives (median delay 262 units); centre in 6/71. A division_off fork at the wound changes F by -0.01 ± 0.08. Late captures were 0.2 when the hotspot was lost.

findings.claim: Under a mid-life motor sign flip (pull becomes push), every column reflex is helpless. An act-plane annulus with ring 1 empty provides a local second pathway: the inner-rim motors push toward the sensed side under the flipped law. Perfect switching between the two pathways would be worth about +2.7 F.
findings.evidence: t10_flip.py (scratch kernel; t_flip ~ U[256, 768] per life). Captures after the flip: 0.1 per life for both the reflex and annulus-norm. With the flip from t0: reflex -1.55 (0 captures), annulus-flip +4.03 (11.7 captures). Unflipped: annulus-norm +8.77 against reflex +8.73. An oracle switcher (norm before the flip, flip after) gets 16.6 captures against 11.1, about +2.72 F. annulus-both loses in both worlds (+1.30 / -1.46), so no fixed body solves it.

findings.claim: BLINK (the target goes dark for stretches) costs the reflex heavily, but none of four hand-built memory variants recovers the loss. Memory does not pass A2 yet. The reasons: a per-cell hold conflicts with fresh evidence elsewhere in the body, and a click needs current evidence.
findings.evidence: t5, reflex@hollow3: 8.67 at base; 5.37 with blink 20/10; 3.65 at 20/20; 1.17 at 10/30. GRN router plus hold genes, against the router twin: naive holds -1.4 to -4.0 F (blink 20/10) and -2.6 to -6.8 (base). Holds cancelled by neighbour evidence: +0.00 ± 0.14 and -0.42. A centre click-hold: +0.10 to +0.16 (± 0.09) at blink 5/5. Flash-then-dim: +0.27 ± 0.10. Stationary blinking targets: at most +0.05.

findings.claim: In LEAD worlds the predictable case is the hard one for pursuit. At the same target speed, straight runs cost the reflex far more than frequent tumbles. A persistence twin gains only where trajectories are predictable.
findings.evidence: t12, reflex@hollow3 at v_t 0.3: 1.92 with tau_turn 200 against 5.71 with tau_turn 5; at v_t 0.2: 5.19 against 7.77. Router minus reflex at v0.3 / tau 200: -0.33 ± 0.12. The hold twin of the GRN router gains +1.20 (unpaired SE about 0.14) over its non-hold twin at v0.3 / tau 200 and +0.83 at v0.2 / tau 200. It loses -0.67 at base and -0.24 to -0.40 when targets tumble.

findings.claim: The b2 keys do not yet give a discrimination world that rewards a circuit. A broad poison that is always present is a cliff. A dim poison is solved by a single cell's rate threshold. Tuned centre-surround veto bodies lose to the re-tuned reflex, including in a world where the peak rates match and only width differs.
findings.evidence: t8: broad poison (p 1, b2_mode 1, -50): reflex 0.56 with 41 poison clicks per life; lateral-inhibition bodies -1.05 to -1.71 against it. Dim poison of the same width: reflex 7.36. t15 (decoy-lite: amp 0.7, sigma 1.5, -25, p 0.3): veto@ring3 tuned -0.75 ± 0.10 against the re-tuned reflex (4.25), and lateral_off leaves it unchanged. t15b/c (same peak: amp 1, sigma 1.2): -0.44 ± 0.11. The tuner left the veto nearly silent (J g_r 0.25 + b 0.5 < 1), which matches C.w1 = 0.

findings.claim: Two literature results support varying worlds that share subtasks, and damage during training for regeneration.
findings.evidence: Kashtan & Alon 2005 (PNAS, doi 10.1073/pnas.0503610102): repeatedly switching between goals built from shared subgoals led to modular networks and network motifs. Kashtan, Noor & Alon 2007 (PNAS, doi 10.1073/pnas.0611630104): the largest speedup came from such modularly varying goals, and it grew with problem difficulty. The six worlds here share sense, pull and click, so they fit that pattern. Mordvintsev et al. 2020 (Distill, 'Growing Neural Cellular Automata'): adding damage during training made regeneration robust, including to damage types never seen in training. Mischiati et al. 2015 (Nature, doi 10.1038/nature14045): dragonfly interception steering is model-driven, using internal models of body dynamics and prey motion.

findings.claim: Engineering gaps and a process note. lifesim.js supports neither the second blob (b2) nor the panel perturbations (kill_t / kill_frac), so POISON and WOUND need JS ports for the playground even though kernel and reference have them. Separately, src/life/build.py and kernel.c changed in the repo during this study (fast mode added). I re-verified that the scratch kernel still matches it.
findings.evidence: lifesim.js line 552 throws for noise_rate, kill_t, stuck_t, drop_p and b2_amp > 0. The repo's build.py / kernel.c were modified at 01:12-01:13 (load(fast)). t2_xcheck.py afterwards: ledger equal with all scratch features off for reflex@hollow3, router@ring4 and s5.

candidates.name: ROUTE-FN: fast, noisy SPECK family
candidates.capability: (1) routing / multi-hop relay
candidates.world_change: Existing keys only. Each life draws lam_bg ~ log-U[0.05, 0.2], and either draws (d0, d_min) from {(1, 0.5), (0.5, 0.25)} or takes d0 0.5 as the new base (N5) and varies lam_bg only. Draws are keyed by (run, generation, life) so common random numbers hold. Base SPECK is kept in 25-50% of lives, and each world is scaled by a fixed constant. No twin, decoy or near placement (each erases the lead). No within-life switch is needed.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: While the target is over the interior, a column reflex cannot steer, because interior act cells have no open face. It also fires a motor for every lone receptor event: at lam_bg 0.2, 85% of the reflex's motor chains start from background events (rec_signal 0.15). Pooled, relayed interior evidence keeps the rim pulling while the target crosses the body. Fast hops make the 2-hop relay arrive while the target is still there.
candidates.minimal_circuit: The router@ring4 circuit. Interior coincidence sensors J (g_r 0.5, b 0.25, emitting on channel 1 only) excite rim sensors S (w1 1.0), which drive the rim motor above them on channel 0. That is a J -> S -> M chain of 2 hops, about one d0 per hop.
candidates.positive_control: hb.speck_body('router@ring4') re-tuned in the world with analysis.tune_knobs (ROUTER_GRID, 150 hill evaluations on 192 lives), against reflex@hollow3 and reflex@ring3 re-tuned the same way (t11_retune.py; knobs in retuned_fastbg.json). The GRN form, hb.router_genome(knobs), shows the circuit can be grown.
candidates.measurement: P.chains / chain_summary on rim motors: rec_other_col and relayed (router 0.58, reflex 0.00 here), latency quantised by hop count (0.50 / 1.01 / 1.52 / 2.01 at d0 0.5), and the lateral J->S CCG 'sharp'. A kernel lateral_off fork must remove at least 50% of the lead over the re-tuned reflex. Pre-registered count: seeds whose best body beats the re-tuned reflex by more than 3 paired SE on 1,024 lives, with lateral_off removing at least 50% of the lead.
candidates.engineering: None in kernel.c, reference.py or lifesim.js: d0, d_min and lam_bg exist in all three. About 40-60 lines in src/life/evaluate.py (per-life task-key draw, extending the envelope) and in the evolve aggregation (fixed per-world constants), plus tests. d0 0.5 re-baselines the gates (N5).
candidates.risks: The lead is narrow in world space: a twin target, near placement or decoy-lite cancels it, and sparse receptors reverse it (-1.28 in the review). A precision capture radius also shrinks it, and fast or straight targets reverse it (v0.3 / tau 200: -0.33). Evolution may still settle on s5-style pooling. Noise makes every capture count less, so selection has less signal per life.
candidates.evidence_or_result: t1 (256 lives, block 1), router minus base-tuned reflex@hollow3: base +1.83 ± 0.20; d0 0.5 +3.34 ± 0.23; lam_bg 0.2 +1.58 ± 0.15; both +2.17 ± 0.17; rho_c 0.5 +0.11. Re-tuned in fast+noisy (512 fresh lives, block 13): reflex@hollow3 +6.32 ± 0.09, router +8.63 ± 0.12, lead +2.31 ± 0.13 (z 17); lateral_off dF -8.33 ± 0.12 (3.6 times the lead). t20 traces (2 lives each, block 24): router M relayed 0.584, reflex 0.000.

candidates.name: BLINK (and FLASH): the target goes dark
candidates.capability: (2) memory / persistence (a candidate job for the hidden planes)
candidates.world_change: New world feature, prototyped in a scratch copy of kernel.c (make_xkernel.py, xbuild.py). The target's receptor emission is gated by an on/off renewal process: visible for Exp(blink_on), dark for Exp(blink_off), with luminance factor dark_amp while dark (0 = fully dark). The target keeps moving and stays capturable. The toggles are world events in world_to (a new hash stream S_BLINK) and are folded into the world hash. FLASH mode: visible for blink_on after every placement, then dark or dim. Per life: blink_off drawn from {off, 10, 20} with blink_on 20. Within the life: the renewal process itself.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: With no evidence there is no pull and no click, so the reflex stalls for every dark gap and loses ground while the target drifts.
candidates.minimal_circuit: A per-sector hold that keeps that column's motor pulling in the dark. It is cleared by a timer, and also whenever fresh evidence appears anywhere in the body. That 'nobody sees it' veto has to be broadcast across the body, so it is a routing problem too. A flood layer in the hidden planes is the natural place for it, since hidden cells are isolated from receptor noise. In BODY-1 a hidden cell hears only the act cell below, so the flood must start from act cells. A centre click-hold is the second component.
candidates.positive_control: Not achieved: this candidate does not pass A2 yet. Four GRN controls were built: hb.router_genome plus SEEN / HOLD / TIRED genes, a neighbour-vetoed hold, a centre click-hold, and both combined (mem.py, mem2.py). The control still needed is the body-wide veto. It needs at least six cell types (S, C, M, K, a flood relay, a holder), so it must be a GRN genome or an extended program table; the five-row program table cannot express it.
candidates.measurement: Captures during dark periods (a scratch ledger column) and within 20 units after the target reappears. The alignment of dark-period pulls with the bearing at dark onset (a new probe column on strokes / traj). hidden_off, genes_blind and lateral_off forks to locate the memory: it should sit in the hidden planes if the flood design is right. Pre-register: the memory body beats the re-tuned reflex by more than 3 SE, and hidden_off (or genes_blind) removes at least 50% of the gain.
candidates.engineering: New keys blink_on, blink_off, dark_amp: an ABI-4 world vector, or reserved slots. About 40 lines each in kernel.c (world event, thinning gate, hash fold), reference.py and lifesim.js. spec.py keys and validation (both means >= 2^-10, dark_amp in [0, 1]). Golden kernel = reference = JS tests. probe.py inherits the feature through _TAcct once the reference has it.
candidates.risks: Measured: holds conflict with current evidence elsewhere in the body, and a click needs evidence, so the payoff is capped. Single-cell gene timers can satisfy simple versions without any circuit, as the prior occlusion result showed (+0.05, matched by a single-cell slow state). Long dark fractions are cliffs: at blink 10/30 the reflex earns 1.17 and the router 0.25.
candidates.evidence_or_result: t5 (256 lives, block 5), reflex@hollow3: 8.67 at base; blink 20/10 5.37; 20/20 3.65; 10/30 1.17; 5/5 3.92; flash6 0.17. Router lead: +0.92, +0.10, -0.93. Memory variants against the GRN-router twin: naive -1.4 to -4.0 (blink 20/10) and -2.6 to -6.8 (base); neighbour-vetoed +0.00 ± 0.14 and -0.42; centre click-hold +0.10 to +0.16 (± 0.09, blink 5/5); flash-dim +0.27 ± 0.10; stationary targets at most +0.05 (t14, t16, t18).

candidates.name: LEAD: fast targets on straight runs (the ladder's 'jump' rung in this world)
candidates.capability: (3) prediction / interception
candidates.world_change: Existing keys. Each life draws v_t from {0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.3} and tau_turn from {5, 20, 200}. Most lives keep v_t <= 0.2 so the reflex still earns (A1). Optional within-life fast, straight phases would need an epoch feature (scalar redraws at Poisson world times). Score the prediction gain as F(tau 200) - F(tau 5) at the same speed, relative to the re-tuned reflex.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Pure pursuit lags the target by a sense-to-pull delay of 1-2 units. On a straight run the target leaves the footprint, and with a 0.6 halo it is then invisible. The reflex therefore does worse on predictable runs than on unpredictable tumbles at the same speed: the predictability goes unused.
candidates.minimal_circuit: A Reichardt or Barlow-Levick direction-selective pair in the sense plane. Sensor B fires the motor one column ahead in the direction of motion, but only if its neighbour A fired about spacing / v_t earlier (a delay line using delta 0.5-2, or a slow membrane). The pull then leads the target, like proportional navigation that steers ahead of the line of sight. A crude version is persistence of the pursuit direction (a hold) through the target's exit.
candidates.positive_control: Partial and built: the hold twin of the GRN router (mem2.mem_genome with tired 4-8, b_hold 0.375, w_near 10) beats its own non-hold twin only on straight runs. Still to build: a direction-selective interceptor. Either use three cell types repeating around the rim (A, B, C program rows, with C also serving as the centre sensor) so each sensor knows its clockwise and counter-clockwise neighbour, or a GRN with direction-specific weights (face weights X1 if approved, or chemistry a_c·ŝ with a chiral morphogen pattern). Tune it with analysis.tune_knobs against the re-tuned reflex.
candidates.measurement: New probe columns. A direction-selectivity index for sense cells: rate when the target moves in the preferred direction against the null direction, conditioned on target position relative to the cell. The pull's lead angle: the signed angle between each stroke and the target bearing, regressed on the target's tangential velocity. Also capture rate against tau_turn at fixed v_t, and a reference Lesion of lateral slots or a delta knockout to remove the delay line.
candidates.engineering: No world change: v_t and tau_turn exist in all three engines. About 60 lines of probe additions. A direction-selective interceptor would need either the face-weight ABI change or careful chemistry.
candidates.risks: v_t 0.3 with straight runs is a cliff (reflex 1.92), so keep it rare. 'Be faster' (more motors, more gain) or persistence may be cheaper for evolution than real prediction. Program mode has only five rows, which limits hand-built direction-selective circuits. The GRN-router base itself is weak here (-2.0 against the reflex at v0.3).
candidates.evidence_or_result: t12 (256 lives, block 14), reflex@hollow3: base 8.78; v0.2 / tau200 5.19; v0.2 / tau5 7.77; v0.3 / tau200 1.92; v0.3 / tau5 5.71. Router minus reflex: -0.33 ± 0.12 at v0.3 / tau200 and +0.55 ± 0.16 at v0.2 / tau200. Hold twin minus GRN router: +1.20 (unpaired SE about 0.14) at v0.3 / tau200; +0.83 at v0.2 / tau200; -0.67 at base; -0.24 and -0.40 when tumbling.

candidates.name: FLIP (and FLIP-CUE): the motor sign flips mid-life
candidates.capability: (4) context switching / within-life adaptation
candidates.world_change: New key t_flip, prototyped in the scratch kernel: strokes at t >= t0 + t_flip apply -g_n (push instead of pull); earlier strokes keep their pull. Per life: 25% flipped from t0 (context across lives, the easier first step), 25% flipped at U[256, 768], 50% unflipped. Signalled variant FLIP-CUE: a harmless broad second blob (b2_value 0) appears at the flip. This needs b2 epochs, also prototyped as e_on / e_off. With the cue, the switch can be read from the senses rather than learned from consequences, which matches the ladder's 'context' rung.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: After the flip, every column reflex pushes its target away, and it has no other pathway.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Two motor pathways per sector and a slow switch for each sector. Outer-rim motors work under the normal law. Inner-rim motors of an act-plane annulus (ring 1 empty, so ring-2 faces point inward) push toward the sensed side under the flipped law, so no cross-body route is needed. Switch rule: a bistable gene with hysteresis, toggled by a slow integrator of failures (targets seen at ring 3 that never reach ring 2) and reset by successes. In FLIP-CUE, cue-detecting sensors set a body-wide context instead, which needs a broadcast.
candidates.positive_control: Built: fixed program-mode annulus bodies (t10_flip.py annulus(mode)). Sensors on rings 2 and 3 plus the centre; act plane K plus rings 2 and 3; the reflex@hollow3 knobs. 'norm' makes the ring-3 motors listen; 'flip' makes the ring-2 motors listen. The oracle bound uses 'norm' before the flip and 'flip' after it. Still to build: the adaptive switcher as a GRN. Grow the annulus with a centre morphogen so ring 2 can be told from ring 3, and add a per-sector toggle gene.
candidates.measurement: The time course of capture rate after t_flip (recovery time). A genes_blind fork at t_flip: if adaptation runs through genes, there should be no recovery. Which pathway is used (twitch counts of ring-2 against ring-3 act cells, via trace_kernel) before and after the flip. The ratio F_post / F_post(oracle).
candidates.engineering: About 5-10 lines each in kernel.c catch_stroke (the sign), reference.py and lifesim.js. A spec key and validation (an ABI bump, or a reserved slot). An optional ledger column for captures after the flip. Tests. FLIP-CUE also needs b2 epochs (about 30 lines per engine) and the b2 port to JS.
candidates.risks: Without the pending local consequence signal (decision 3, capture and miss bits at the tap cell), unsignalled flips may be unlearnable, which is why the cue variant and flipped-from-t0 lives come first. The annulus is itself a morphology that evolution has to find. Mid-life flips halve the base signal.
candidates.evidence_or_result: t10 (256 lives, block 10). Unflipped: reflex 8.73, annulus-norm 8.77, annulus-flip -1.68. Flipped from t0: reflex -1.55 (0 captures), annulus-flip +4.03 ± 0.12 (11.7 captures). Mid-life flip: reflex 3.76 and annulus-norm 3.70, with 0.1 captures after the flip; annulus-both 0.01. Oracle switcher: 16.6 captures against 11.1, about +2.72 F.

candidates.name: POISON: a same-peak broad poison blob (two blob types)
candidates.capability: (5) discrimination: approach one kind of target, refuse another
candidates.world_change: Existing b2 keys: b2_amp 1.0, b2_sigma 1.2, b2_value -25, b2_mode 0 (placed with the target). The peak event rate per cell equals the target's, so only spatial extent separates the two, which needs neighbours. Each life draws b2_p from {0, 0.3, 0.5}. Never b2_p 1 with b2_mode 1: that is a cliff. Later, a blob-type table could retire the special b2 keys.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: The reflex pulls toward any light and clicks on any centred blob: 24-33 poison clicks per life here, and 38-68 in the decoy-lite variants. Its time and captures are diverted to the poison.
candidates.minimal_circuit: A centre-surround veto on the click: interior sensors relay surround activity on channel 1 to the centre sensor C, which is inhibited (C.w1 < 0), so a broad blob vetoes the click. Lateral inhibition with matched timing among rim sensors keeps the body from approaching. Later, an approach-or-avoid choice through the annulus pathways (see AVOID).
candidates.positive_control: Built and not passing: veto@ring3, a role body with the J row emitting channel 1 and C.w1 tuned (t15_veto_tune.py, t15b_veto_tune.py, t15c_eval.py), tuned over 150 evaluations against the re-tuned reflex. Still to try: rim lateral inhibition with time-matched windows; a surround veto fed by ring-1 and ring-2 sensors through a hidden relay; the annulus avoid pathway.
candidates.measurement: Poison clicks against captures (a discrimination ratio). P.tuning per blob (rate against distance to blob 0 and to blob 1). A lateral_off fork, or C.w1 set to 0: if the circuit works, poison clicks must come back. A negative J->C CCG at about one hop.
candidates.engineering: The kernel and reference already have b2. lifesim.js lacks b2 and needs a port of about 80-100 lines: placement, turns, timer, presence, thinning, click outcome. Per-life draws as in ROUTE-FN.
candidates.risks: Measured: a broad poison that is always present is a cliff (reflex 0.56, and -0.57 in decoy-lite p 0.5). A dim poison is solved by a single cell's rate threshold. Fixed lateral inhibition costs 2.6-6 F in base. So far A2 fails in both worlds tested. The review's point stands: fixed discrimination costs in easy situations, so it may pay only as a context-gated (adaptive) circuit.
candidates.evidence_or_result: t8 (256 lives, block 8): broad poison (p 1, mode 1, -50) reflex 0.56; lateral-inhibition bodies -1.05 to -1.71 against it; dim poison of the same width: reflex 7.36, router 8.81. t13: decoy-lite (amp 0.7, p 0.3, -25) reflex 3.96, router 4.13, s5 2.09. t15 (512 lives): veto -0.75 ± 0.10 against the re-tuned reflex (4.25); lateral_off on the veto gives 3.53, no difference. t15c (same peak, 512 lives, block 25): re-tuned reflex 4.49; veto -0.44 ± 0.11; the veto body with C.w1 = 0 gives 4.19.

candidates.name: WOUND: cells lost mid-life
candidates.capability: (6) regeneration / size regulation (and a job for genome-driven death)
candidates.world_change: Existing panel keys kill_t and kill_frac, drawn per life: 50% unwounded, the rest with kill_t ~ U[256, 768] and kill_frac in {0.25, 0.5}. Later, the reserved kill_rate (a per-cell Poisson hazard, with refill through the existing claims) for repeated wounds within one life, and kill_frac as a family axis.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: The reflex cannot regrow. In 44% of lives it loses the hotspot or the centre sensor and makes no further captures. In the rest it loses about 58% of its capture rate with the missing rim cells.
candidates.minimal_circuit: A local hole detector in sense cells that were interior, active only after development. The cell divides into its own empty slot: up if its act cell died, else into the hole. Roles come back from local cues. The centre sensor re-divides upward to regrow the hotspot, and the hotspot accepts a relay-type centre.
candidates.positive_control: Built: regen7.regen_genome(router knobs plus K.w1 = 1) in regen7.py. It is hb.router_genome with gene 7 (INNER) made slow (lambda 1/16) and four genes added. GATE: the lineage timer is past 0.5. MAT: maturity, with Q -1. FULL: all 7 contacts present. LOSS = sigma(20·INNER - 20·FULL + 20·GATE + 20·MAT - 50), feeding p_div. Router gene 12 (quiet) is freed for this.
candidates.measurement: From kernel fate logs: the share of killed sites refilled by T, the hotspot and centre regrowth rate and delay, and captures after the wound. A division_off fork at kill_t gives the value of regrowth. Final size against pre-wound size checks for overgrowth. An apoptosis knockout tests whether death gets a job.
candidates.engineering: None in the kernel or reference: kill_t and kill_frac exist. lifesim.js lacks panel perturbations, so the KILL event needs a port of about 30 lines. The per-life draw goes in evaluate.py. kill_rate (reserved for v2) would need a new handler of about 40 lines in each of the three engines, plus an ABI note.

Inherited slow memories cause regrowth cascades (measured). Wounds could select bigger, redundant bodies instead of regrowth; the division_off fork tells the two apart. Wounding at T/2 in half the lives adds noise to the base signal.

candidates.name: AVOID: a stinging blob (the ladder's 'withdraw' rung in this world)
candidates.capability: (1) routing plus (5) discrimination: move away from one kind of blob, toward another
candidates.world_change: New feature. Blob 1 stings: it charges c_sting per unit time while the dot is within b2_rho of it, computed in closed form by the accountant from the dot's and the blob's paths, or approximated by a cost each time the dot enters the zone. Its b2_amp and b2_sigma differ from the target's. Per life: the stinger is present in 50% of lives. Unlike POISON, this rewards moving away, not just withholding the click.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: The reflex pulls toward every light, so it sits in the sting zone and keeps paying.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Threat evidence must drive motors that move the body away. One way is across the body: the opposite rim, a chain the length of the diameter (the withdraw rung). The other is local: the inner-rim motors of an annulus, whose faces point inward, so under the normal law they pull away from the sensed side. Either way, a discriminating sensor rule decides which pathway each event drives.
candidates.positive_control: Partial: the annulus-flip body from t10, run in the normal world, earns 0 captures. Its inner pathway reliably moves the body away from whatever it senses. To build: combine the outer pathway for narrow, bright food with the inner pathway for broad threats, and tune it against the re-tuned reflex.
candidates.measurement: Time spent inside b2_rho and the sting cost paid. Chains from threat-tuned sensors to inner-rim or opposite-rim motors (P.chains, extended to record which blob caused the origin event). lateral_off should remove avoidance if the route crosses the body, and leave it intact if it is the local annulus.
candidates.engineering: About 30 lines each in the kernel accountant and in reference.py. The JS engine needs the b2 port first (about 100 lines in total). New spec keys and an ABI bump.
candidates.risks: The closed-form time-in-zone calculation is fiddly. The local annulus route may turn this into a morphology task rather than a routing task. The discrimination step has not yet been shown to pay (see POISON).
candidates.evidence_or_result: t10: the annulus-flip body in the normal world scores -1.68 with 0 captures per life, so a withdrawing pathway exists. t8 / t13: reflexes are drawn to blob 1 (24-68 clicks on it per life).

findings.claim: The niche map ran on existing world keys only. It covers 48 world cells: base catch_speck_l4, 35 one-axis cells (sigma, lam_bg, lam_s, v_t, tau_turn, R_min/R_max, t_resp, c_miss, T, six b2 decoy and second-food settings, kill_frac at t 512, d0 0.5) and 12 combinations. Each cell has paired F on 512 shared lives for every body. On top of that, 12 cells were confirmed on 1,024 fresh lives with the router re-tuned too.
findings.evidence: Lives: evaluation 40,200,000+s; confirmation 40,220,000+s; tuning 40,250,000/40,260,000+s; probe traces 40,230,000+s; timing 40,290,000+s. Bodies: hand reflex@hollow3, a reflex re-tuned per cell (screen of the 6 frozen SPECK reflex shapes, then an 80-evaluation coordinate ascent on 128 tuning lives), router@ring4 frozen and re-tuned per cell (45 evaluations, 96 tuning lives; not run for c_miss and T=2048), s5, s7, and the A1 references (lone cell, clicker, S0 champion). Each of router, s5 and s7 has a pair of twins forked at t 256 (unchanged and lateral_off), both counted over [256, T]. Base check: router minus best reflex +2.37+-0.14 (1,024 fresh lives +2.26+-0.10), against +2.17 in the design review. Router lateral_off share 0.87; s5 0.66, s7 0.85 (pilot: 63% and 86%).

findings.claim: Routing pays most with bright targets (lam_s 4), fast conduction (d0 0.5), slow targets (v_t 0.05), low noise (lam_bg 0.0125) and long target stays (t_resp 100-200). These levers add up to more than the sum of their parts. In every one of these cells the router's lead is carried by lateral messages.

Router minus best reflex, 512 lives (re-tuned router in brackets):

Super-additive: lam_s 4 alone adds +0.7 over base and d0 0.5 alone +1.4, but together they add +4.0. In all of these cells lateral_off removes 0.71-0.92 of the router's post-256 F, which is 2.3-3.9 times its post-256 lead. Not re-tuning the router does not change this ranking.

findings.claim: Settings that remove routing's advantage: wide halos, sparse receptor events, targets placed near or far, short target stays, a second food blob, decoys and mid-life kills. Wide halos also break the frozen router; when re-tuned it wins again, but as a bigger reflex rather than by routing.

c_miss 2-20 (+2.36 to +2.37) and T 512-2048 (+2.34 to +2.50) leave the lead unchanged.

findings.claim: Small, bright targets (sigma 0.4, lam_s 4, best with d0 0.5) are the only worlds where the evolved bodies beat the best reflex. Every body there depends almost entirely on lateral messages, and the re-tuned router leads by about 5.6 on top. This makes it a continuous path from pooling to routing.
findings.evidence:
sigma0.4+lam_s4+d0 0.5, 1,024 fresh lives:
- best reflex +4.89
- s5 +6.17, lead +1.28+-0.08
- s7 +5.39, lead +0.50+-0.08
- re-tuned router +10.50, lead +5.61+-0.10
- lateral_off removes 0.86 (s5), 0.94 (s7) and 1.05 (router) of post-256 F
sigma0.4+lam_s4 without d0 0.5: s5 +0.28+-0.08, router +2.91+-0.09 (fresh lives); with v_t 0.05: s5 +0.39+-0.12 (512 lives). A1 holds in these cells (clicker z +10 to +18; champion z +30 to +39). In base, s5 trails the reflex by 1.42 and s7 by 1.79.

findings.claim: Across worlds, the evolved bodies do best against the reflex where they rely most on lateral messages. The router does best in a different set of worlds: those where the evolved bodies rely least on lateral messages. So evolution's pooling optimum and routing are rewarded in different parts of world space.
findings.evidence:
Spearman over the 41 cells where the bodies earn:
- s5 lead vs s5 lateral_off share: +0.70 (permutation p < 0.001)
- re-tuned router lead vs s5 lateral share: -0.34 (p 0.03)
- re-tuned router lead vs s7 lateral share: -0.29 (p 0.06)
- router lead vs s5 lead: +0.03 (p 0.86)
In the strongest routing cells (lam_s 4 combinations), s5's lateral share falls to 0.38-0.47 and it trails the reflex by 3.0-4.4. It is highest in sparse-evidence cells: lam_s 0.5 2.84, v_t 0.3 1.52, sigma 0.4 1.34, R 3-8 1.18.

findings.claim: Probe chains show that s7 is already a multi-hop relay body. 62-67% of its rim-motor spikes started from a receptor event in another column, with latency set by hop count. That is a stronger routing signature than the hand router's, but s7's F still trails the reflex in base. The router's relayed share rises in the bright-target worlds.
findings.evidence:
P.trace on 4 lives per body per world, every trace checked bitwise against the kernel; chains/*.json. Share of rim-motor receptor-origin chains with at least one in-plane hop:
- router: base 0.358, lam_s4 0.466, triple combination 0.445, d0 0.5 0.354, sigma 0.4 0.277
- s5: base 0.314, lam_s4 0.370, triple 0.392, sigma 0.4 0.223
- s7: 0.620-0.675 in all 7 worlds, chains up to 12 hops; sense spikes fired by lateral arrivals 0.46-0.52
Latency per hop: 1.0/2.0/3.0 at d0 1, and 0.49/1.0/1.49 at d0 0.5, for all three bodies.

findings.claim: Selection information per CPU-second for telling the router from the reflex (z^2 bought per CPU-second) is 3-4x the base value in the routing worlds, and near zero in dense or sparse worlds. Per-life SD of F stays at about 1.4-4.4 everywhere.
findings.evidence:
z^2 per CPU-s = (mean paired difference / per-life SD)^2 / CPU of the two lives. CPU comes from a cost model fitted to single-thread timing passes: 401 ns per heap event + 0.24 us per tick + 160 ns per receptor candidate; measured/model IQR 0.90-1.34. Raw timings on the loaded laptop varied 0.54-1.13x between passes, and the c_miss cells, which are identical lives, varied 68-96 ms.
Router lead, frozen / re-tuned router:
- base 5.5 / 6.1
- triple combination 20.1 / 20.4
- lam_s4+d0 16.0
- v_t0.05+d0 15.7 / 18.2
- d0 0.5 11.8 / 16.3
- sigma0.4+lam_s4+d0: re-tuned 22.7
- T 512 6.5; T 2048 5.4
- twin food 0.1, lam_s 1 0.1, R 1-4 0.3, decoy-dim 0.6
Same contrast for s5 lateral_off: 0.1 (lam_bg 0.2 + lam_s 4) to 27 (R 1-4); base 16.
Ranges per life: SD of F reference reflex 0.6-3.8, router 1.2-4.5, s5 1.0-3.4; captures reference 0.9-63, router 4-58, s5 2-42; model CPU reference 13-54 ms, router 34-136 ms, s5 35-222 ms (b2 blobs and wide halos raise it through lambda_max and spikes).

findings.claim: Mid-life kills mostly test whether the single hotspot column survives. The hand bodies cannot regrow it, the GRN router genome barely regrows, and s5 partly regrows it. This is a separate niche for regeneration.
findings.evidence:
kill_t 512, 256 lives, F counted after the kill. Share of lives with 0 captures after the kill:
- hand reflex: 49% (25% kill) / 82% (50% kill); post-kill F +1.03 / -0.30
- s5: 27% / 44%; post-kill F +1.91 / -0.25; births 131 / 144 vs 120 with no kill
- GRN router genome (handbuilt.router_genome, 128 lives): 34% / 60%; only 3-5 births; post-kill F -0.38 / -0.71
Whole-life: s5's deficit to the reflex shrinks from -1.42 to -0.60 / -0.98, and the router lead falls to +0.74 / +0.86.

findings.claim: The existing b2 decoys do not create a discrimination niche. The re-tuned reflex wins by clicking less, and routers lose more because their relays spread decoy evidence. Second food blobs make the world dense, which helps the reflex.
findings.evidence: Decoy-lite (b2_amp 1, b2_sigma 1.5, value -50, b2_p 0.5): hand reflex -0.31; re-tuned reflex +1.74, with decoy clicks per life down from 65 to 8.5; router +0.72; s5 -0.34. On fresh lives the re-tuned router is -0.92+-0.06. Decoy-wide (always present, -100): every body is negative; the champion fails A1 (z -171) and so does the clicker (z -4). Twin food: router lead +0.45, s5 -3.59.

findings.claim: Both reference bodies have to be re-tuned in each world before a cell can be judged. The frozen router and the frozen reflex mislead in most shifted worlds.
findings.evidence: Reflex re-tune gains on the tuning lives: up to +5.6 (sigma 1.5) and +4.1 (decoy-wide); on fresh lives decoy-wide went from -10.4 to -1.7. Re-tuning the router turns the lead from negative to positive in 4 cells (sigma 0.9, sigma 1.5, v_t 0.3, v_t 0.3+d0 0.5) and to about 0 at lam_s 0.5 (-1.34 to -0.01). Re-tunes moved mostly the click knob C.g_r and the interior gain J.g_r (0.5 to 0.625).

findings.claim: Literature (opened): goals that vary in a modular way, with shared subproblems, speed evolution and build modular, reusable structure. Randomly varying goals do not. Connection costs also favour modularity. This supports a task family drawn from inside the measured routing and pooling region, rather than random or wide variety.
findings.evidence: Kashtan & Alon 2005, PNAS, 'Spontaneous evolution of modularity and network motifs' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1236541/): modular Qm 0.54 vs 0.12 with fixed goals; about 1,400 vs 9,000 generations to a solution; random goals gave no modularity. Parter, Kashtan & Alon 2008, PLoS Comput Biol, 'Facilitated variation' (https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000206): structured variation generalises to unseen goals. Clune, Mouret & Lipson 2013, Proc R Soc B (https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.2743): connection costs drive modularity and evolvability.

candidates.name: ROUTE-FAST world (bright, slow targets, fast conduction)
candidates.capability: (1) routing / multi-hop relay
candidates.world_change: Existing keys only, on catch_speck_l4: lam_s 4.0, v_t 0.05, d0 0.5, d_min 0.25. A milder variant uses lam_s 4 + d0 0.5 and keeps v_t 0.1.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: When the target sits over interior sense cells, their act cells cannot pull, so the reflex only steers once the target reaches the rim columns. With bright targets and fast hops, relaying interior evidence to the rim motors pays before the target leaves.
candidates.minimal_circuit: The hand router: interior coincidence sensors J relay on ch1, rim sensors S (w1 1.0) pass to rim motors M. It works in 1-2 lateral hops.
candidates.positive_control: router@ring4 with frozen knobs (handbuilt.speck_body('router@ring4')). On 1,024 fresh lives it leads the best reflex by +6.96+-0.15 in the triple world and +6.52+-0.14 at lam_s4+d0. The re-tuned router (confirm.py) leads by +7.10+-0.14.
candidates.measurement:
- Lead of the body over the re-tuned reflex
- lateral_off share at t 256 (router 0.83, which is 2.5x its lead)
- P.chains on rim motors: relayed share and rec_other_col (router 0.445 here vs 0.358 in base), with latency quantised at 0.5 per hop
- z^2 per CPU-s of the lead: 20 vs 5.5 in base
candidates.engineering: None for a trial: all are world keys. Adopting d0 0.5 as the base re-baselines gates GS1-GS6 (the N5 re-tune gate).
candidates.risks:
- The evolved bodies trail the reflex by 3.8-3.9 here, and their lateral reliance drops to 0.42-0.43. The pooling path evolution follows does not climb toward routing in this world, so the GS3 valley may stay.
- Bright targets make the reflex richer (+13.6), which may favour bigger plain reflexes.
- Paired SD is about 4.4.
candidates.evidence_or_result: 512 lives: +7.20+-0.20 (re-tuned router +7.31). Fresh 1,024: +6.96+-0.15. Router lateral_off share 0.83; s5 0.42, s7 0.59. Model CPU per life: router 91 ms, reflex 34 ms.

candidates.name: POOL-SPECK world (small bright halo plus fast conduction)
candidates.capability: (1) routing, reached through lateral evidence pooling that already beats the reflex
candidates.world_change: Existing keys: sigma 0.4, lam_s 4.0, d0 0.5, d_min 0.25 on catch_speck_l4. Without d0, the variant is sigma 0.4 + lam_s 4.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: A 0.4 halo covers about one sense cell, so evidence in one column is sparse and noisy. Pooling neighbour evidence, and then relaying it to the rim, is needed. Every body loses most or all of its F without lateral messages.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Step 1: neighbour-voting or cooperative sensors with weak lateral excitation, as in s4/s5. Step 2: a one-hop J to S relay to the rim motors, as in the router. Each step pays on its own.
candidates.positive_control: Evolved s5 (P.load('speck_lmax4_hexprism_sex_s5')) leads the best reflex by +1.28+-0.08 on 1,024 fresh lives; s7 by +0.50+-0.08. The re-tuned router reaches +10.50, a lead of +5.61+-0.10, which leaves about +4.3 of headroom for routing above pooling.
candidates.measurement:
- Lead over the re-tuned reflex for evolved bests
- lateral_off share (0.86-1.15 today)
- P.chains relayed share (s5 0.27 today; the router reaches 0.33-0.36)
- Whether the relayed share and the lead grow toward the router's over generations
candidates.engineering: None (world keys). A seeded or unseeded SPECK run in this world is a config change.
candidates.risks:
- Lower F levels (reflex 4.9) and about 13 captures per life, so the per-life SD of about 2 is large next to the gains.
- Evolution may stop at pooling, a local optimum that already beats the reflex.
- Fast conduction re-baselines the gates.
- Small-halo worlds slightly raise cost per life (s5 76-87 ms).
candidates.evidence_or_result: 512 lives: s5 +1.17+-0.12, s7 +0.38, re-tuned router +5.24+-0.14. Fresh 1,024: s5 +1.28+-0.08, s7 +0.50+-0.08, router_rt +5.61+-0.10. A1: clicker z +18, champion z +33. z^2 per CPU-s of the router lead: 22.7 (re-tuned).

candidates.name: Task family per life inside the routing and pooling region
candidates.capability: (1) routing that generalises; partly (4) adaptation across worlds
candidates.world_change: Per-life draw of existing keys through the harness's per-life world envelope (evaluate.py _envelope, keyed by run, generation and life, so CRN holds): sigma in {0.4, 0.6}, lam_s in [2, 4], v_t in [0.05, 0.3], t_resp in [50, 100], with d0 0.5 fixed. Keep base at 25-50% of lives. Exclude wide halos (sigma >= 0.9), twin or second food, and near placement, where the reflex wins or the best router is just a big reflex. Scale F per world by a fixed constant.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Across this region the reflex always trails the re-tuned router by +1.2 to +7.3 F. Each world needs lateral messages: lateral_off removes 0.7-1.2 of the router's F. Fast targets with d0 0.5 add a world where only relays keep up: re-tuned router +3.35, reflex at about half its base F.
candidates.minimal_circuit: The router's J to S to M relay. Its interior gain must work across halo sizes; the re-tunes chose J.g_r 0.625 in most shifted worlds against 0.5 in base.
candidates.positive_control: Re-tuned router per world (router_rt.py) and the frozen router@ring4: the lead is positive in every intended cell. sigma 0.4: +1.72. v_t 0.3+d0: +3.35. lam_s 2-4 with d0: +4.7 to +7.3.
candidates.measurement:
- Per-world lead and lateral share of evolved bests, against the re-tuned reflex of each world
- Chain relayed share
- A held-out combination, for example v_t 0.2 + sigma 0.5
- s5-style lateral-share guard (no drop below base)
candidates.engineering: Harness only, about 30-60 lines in evaluate.py (add the keys to the envelope draw). No kernel, reference.py or lifesim.js change, since every key already exists.
candidates.risks:
- Normalisation choices matter: high-F worlds (lam_s 4) dominate a raw mean.
- Variety in dense worlds selects 'be smaller'; keep twin and food worlds out.
- Mixed worlds add per-life variance.
- Kashtan & Alon (2005) found that random variation, unlike modularly varying goals, gives no structure, so the family should share subproblems (one shared routing task at different scales).
candidates.evidence_or_result: Niche map: in the 12 cells drawn from this region the re-tuned router leads by +1.2 to +7.3, with lateral_off removing 2-4x the lead. Cells excluded for good reason: sigma 0.9/1.5 (re-tuned router lateral share 0.31/0.00), twin food (+0.45), R 1-4 (+0.78 frozen).

candidates.name: WOUND-512 (mid-life kill)
candidates.capability: (6) regeneration and size regulation; gives genome-driven death and division a job
candidates.world_change: Existing panel keys kill_t 512 and kill_frac 0.25-0.5. A per-life random kill time could come through the harness envelope. The reserved kill_rate (Poisson loss) would need kernel.c, reference.py, lifesim.js and an ABI bump.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: The single hotspot column (0,0,0)/(0,0,1) is a point of failure. Losing either cell ends all clicking: 49% of hand-reflex lives (25% kill) and 82% (50% kill) make no capture after the kill. A reflex that cannot regrow cannot recover.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Release of contact inhibition: a cell whose n_view drops below full re-opens division (raises p_div) toward the empty neighbour site, refilling the centre column with the right roles. These are the existing grow/kin genes of column_genome, gated by n_view.
candidates.positive_control: None exists yet. The GRN router genome barely regrows: 3-5 births, 34%/60% zero-capture lives, post-kill F -0.38. s5 partly regrows: 27%/44% zero-capture lives; post-kill F +1.91 vs the reflex's +1.03. A hand-built regrowing column genome (column_genome with the grow gene re-armed by n_view < 7/8) should be built and must beat the non-regrowing genome after the wound first.
candidates.measurement:
- Births after the kill, time until (0,0,1) is re-occupied, post-kill captures and share of zero-capture lives
- division_off fork at kill_t + 1 as the lesion (its paired dF is the value of regrowth)
- n_end recovery
candidates.engineering: None for a fixed kill time; it is already a panel perturbation and in all three engines. A per-life kill time is harness only. kill_rate needs a kernel, reference and JS change plus a new ABI version.
candidates.risks:
- It may select 'regrow one site quickly' rather than circuit computation.
- The fixed hotspot (Q6) makes the world brittle.
- Kills lower F for every body, compressing the leads (router lead falls to +0.74).
candidates.evidence_or_result:
512 lives, whole life:
- reflex 4.89 / 4.16 (kill 25% / 50%) against 8.43 with no kill
- s5 4.29 / 3.18 against 7.03
- router 5.64 / 5.02
- lateral_off share of s5 0.91-1.00
Post-kill window (256 lives): reflex zero-capture 0.49/0.82, s5 0.27/0.44.

candidates.capability: (3) prediction / interception; relay speed first
candidates.world_change: Existing keys: v_t 0.3, d0 0.5, d_min 0.25. Optionally tau_turn 0 (straight runs) for a later interception test.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: The target leaves its halo within a few hop delays. The reflex at v_t 0.3 keeps only 38% of its base F (3.25 vs 8.45), and the re-tuned reflex 4.78 even with d0 0.5.

candidates.positive_control: Re-tuned router (S.g_r 1.0, J.g_r 0.625, J.w1 0.25): +8.12, a lead of +3.35+-0.13 at v_t 0.3+d0 0.5, with lateral_off share 0.99. A hand-built interceptor is not built, so prediction itself is unproven.

- P.tuning offset pref - own and pull lead angle against the target heading
- Chain latency
- For interception: the lead after a delay_line lesion (a fork setting delta to 0)

- The frozen router fails here (-0.51), so results depend on tuning.

candidates.evidence_or_result: v_t 0.3: frozen router -0.52, re-tuned +1.00. v_t 0.3 + d0 0.5: frozen -0.51, re-tuned +3.35+-0.13. s5 lateral share at v_t 0.3: 1.52.

candidates.name: Discrimination with b2 decoys (negative result for the existing keys)
