candidates.evidence_or_result: Design only. Confirmed by reading evolve_life: gen is the only generator; ev.draw, recheck_draw and the T draw are stateless.

candidates.name: (a) task family drawn per life, with fixed per-world normalisation
candidates.capability: Generalisation across worlds, and lets a wound, decoy, flip or blink world be an axis instead of a stage.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: It need not fail. The family is the container. The pilot showed twin- and decoy-heavy families select 'be smaller', so each member must pass the niche gate first.
candidates.minimal_circuit: n/a
candidates.positive_control: Per member: the best hand body (reflex, router, or a role body re-tuned in that member) sets the scale. A member enters only if some reference earns F > 0 there; every decoy world currently fails this (all references negative).
candidates.measurement: Per-member raw F and normalised F for best and references; the share of F that lateral_off removes per member (guard: s5's share must not fall below base); member shares of selection lives.
candidates.engineering: About 60-80 lines in evaluate.py (draw/columns), about 40 in evolve.py/run.py reporting (per-member valid, final table), plus config validation (kill_t < min T_choices) and tests (CRN equality, recheck alignment, normalisation identity, shares): 2 person-days. Scale measurement: about 5 bodies x 1,024 lives x 0.1 s, about 9 CPU-min per member (0.5 day of scripting). Prototype fam_eval.py (about 110 lines) already runs inside evolve_life.
candidates.risks: Normalisation by small scales amplifies noise (SD/scale). An additive offset cancels under CRN, so only the scale matters for selection. Keep scales fixed, never population ranks: ranks detach cell cost from F. Not in lifesim.js until the b2/KILL ports.
candidates.evidence_or_result: exp6: FamilyEvaluator smoke inside unmodified evolve_life with the recheck: shares 0.508 / 0.240 / 0.252 for 2:1:1, recheck members aligned, CRN identical F, F_norm x scale = F_raw.

candidates.name: (b) within-life epochs: two-state telegraph of accountant-side world keys
candidates.capability: Context switching and within-life adaptation (capability 4), and the machinery for (c), (d), (e) and fast phases (h).
candidates.why_reflex_fails: A fixed reflex has one mapping, so it loses whatever the B state penalises: flip -5.5 F, blink 20/20 -5.0 F, payoff swap -12.5 F for reflex@hollow3. Any recovery needs state held across time (gene drift, latch) or cue-gated routing.
candidates.minimal_circuit: A cue detector (e.g. a cell integrating background events, or reading the receptor trace through the GRN) gating which of two reflex mappings is active. For a flip, a crossed mapping: the sense cell drives the motor on the opposite side (a routing relay).
candidates.positive_control: Hand role body with two arcs (ipsilateral pull, contralateral via a lateral relay) and a cue-gated inhibitory switch, built from ROUTER_GRID knobs (router relay channel 1 plus inhibition). It must beat both the re-tuned reflex and the fixed contralateral body across the mixture by more than 3 SE before any evolution run (L2 gate).
candidates.measurement: dF against base by state (per-state ledger columns); recovery curve of the capture rate after each switch (probe trace); genes_blind or freeze fork after a switch to show adaptation is in-life; lateral_off share.
candidates.engineering: Kernel: +86/-11 lines for the whole bundle incl. flicker (prototype, compiles warning-free). reference.py: about +70-95 (prototype xref.py). spec.py: +12 World fields, validation, STREAMS. LIFE_ABI.md: 3, 4.7, 9.6, 9.7.1/3/4/5 and new section-15 entries. Tests: neutrality on golden lives, kernel = reference on random lives per feature, window = heap, ledger identity under swap, telegraph statistics, flicker boundaries. Sizes pinned to 66 in test_life_spec_abi3.py:35/197/214/240/247 and test_life_handbuilt.py:351 must change. Effort: about 3.5-4 person-days without JS; JS +1 day after its b2/KILL prerequisites (+1-1.5 days). Needs an ABI number: world keys only, no genome change.
candidates.risks: Value or flip switches are not learnable without a cue or a local consequence signal (no cell sees income; a flip is visible only through sensorimotor consequences). A background-rate cue doubles misses (exp4). Epochs of 100 units against GRN adaptation on 10-100 units may be too fast. lambda_max raises CPU.
candidates.evidence_or_result: Off: 1,120 lives bitwise against the repo kernel. On: 90/90 lives kernel = reference bitwise, 16/16 scheduler and tie invariance. Effects (exp4): flip100 reflex -5.48±0.26 / router -7.65 / s5 -5.33. With the bg x6 cue: misses x2.

candidates.name: (c) blinking target (memory / persistence)
candidates.capability: Memory: activity that bridges an invisible interval. A job for hidden planes.
candidates.world_change: Pure config after (b): ep_amp0 = 0 in state B (e.g. ep_tau_a 40, ep_tau_b 10). Candidate streams are unchanged (only acceptance changes); the target still moves and can be captured while dark; the timer keeps re-placing. Standalone without (b): about 1.5-2 person-days in all three engines.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: A reflex steers only while receptor events arrive, so captures fall with the dark fraction (reflex -2.09 at 20% dark, -5.02 at 50%).
candidates.minimal_circuit: A self-sustaining loop (a hidden-plane or lateral reverberating pair, or the post-spike latch at v = 0 above rest) that keeps the last-active rim motor twitching for about tau_B, then decays.
candidates.positive_control: reflex@hollow3 plus a hidden cell above each rim act cell, with mutual excitation and a slow leak, so motor drive persists about 10 units after its sense cell goes quiet. It must beat the re-tuned reflex by at least 3 SE in the blink world; note the earlier occlusion test gained only +0.05.
candidates.measurement: Capture rate inside dark intervals and within 5 units after; hidden_off fork cost; chains with hidden-plane origin; act spikes during dark intervals with no receptor ancestor (P.chains origin 'resid' or 'tonic').
candidates.engineering: Config once (b) exists. Probe: log switch times (word 14).
candidates.risks: Slow targets (v_t 0.1) move only about 1 unit in 10, so 'stay put' may already be near-optimal and leave no headroom. The timer re-placement during darkness makes memory worthless in those intervals.
candidates.evidence_or_result: exp4: blink40_10 reflex -2.09±0.23, router -3.11, s5 -2.06. blink20_20 reflex -5.02, router -7.29, s5 -4.88. Upper bound on recoverable headroom is 2-7 F.

candidates.name: (d) motor sign flip mid-life
candidates.capability: Within-life adaptation of the sensorimotor map, possibly with routing (a contralateral relay).
candidates.world_change: Pure config after (b): ep_motor = -1 (g_eff = g_n x ep_motor at stroke time). Residual pulls are stored signed, so a death removes them exactly. Optional context cue ep_bg, or a background flicker key (about 5 more lines).
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Every twitch drives the dot away from the target in state B: reflex 0 captures when always flipped, -5.48 F at 100/100 dwell.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Sense cell to the opposite-side rim motor through a lateral relay (at least 2 hops across the body) enabled by a cue detector; or, without a cue, a slow gene-level sign switch driven by 'halo recedes after my twitch' (needs plasticity or a consequence signal).
candidates.positive_control: The two-arc cue-gated role body of (b), with the fixed contralateral-only body and the reflex as references. Build it by adding a ring-crossing relay to router@ring4 (J relay on channel 1 to the opposite rim).
candidates.measurement: Per-state captures; P.chain_summary rec_other_col and relayed share in state B; lateral_off removes most of the B-state F; latency quantised by hops.
candidates.engineering: Config after (b).
candidates.risks: Without a cue it may be unlearnable within a life under the current rules. With a background cue the cue itself costs misses.
candidates.evidence_or_result: exp4: flip100 dF reflex -5.48±0.26, router -7.65, s4 -3.93, s5 -5.33, s7 -4.98. Always flipped: reflex F -1.53 (0 captures).

candidates.name: (e) which blob pays switches mid-life
candidates.capability: Context-dependent discrimination: approach in one context, avoid in the other.
candidates.world_change: Pure config after (b): ep_swap = 1. In B the target pays b2_value and blob 1 pays R_cap. Ledger semantics: captures = rewarded clicks and b2_clicks = the other blob, so close_life's cost identity holds with no new columns. Works with one blob ('poison phase': the target costs b2_value in B) or two, which must differ by a local cue (b2_sigma, b2_amp or flicker).
candidates.why_reflex_fails: The reflex clicks whatever is under it: swap+cue+big decoy -12.5 F, poison phase -8.3 F.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Cue detector x blob-type detector (center-surround for size, or a temporal filter for flicker) gating the click cell (C to K) through inhibition.
candidates.positive_control: reflex@hollow3 plus a cue-integrating cell that inhibits the hotspot driver when the cue is on, re-tuned on the ROUTER_GRID channel-1 inhibition knobs. It must beat the reflex by at least 3 SE.
candidates.measurement: Per-state rewarded and penalised clicks; clicks on the penalised blob per unit time in each state; lesion of the cue pathway.
candidates.engineering: Config after (b). Needs a cue: without one, no cell can observe value, because a hit on either blob re-places it and looks identical.
candidates.risks: Unlearnable without a cue or a consequence signal (a pending user decision). A bg cue raises misses.
candidates.evidence_or_result: exp4: swap_cue_big reflex -12.52±0.71, router -10.93, s5 -12.28, s7 -16.04. poison_phase_cue reflex -8.32, s5 -7.63.

candidates.name: (f) wound world (cells lost mid-life)
candidates.capability: Regeneration and size regulation; gives genome-driven death and regrowth a job.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Program role bodies do not divide, so they never regrow (0% regrown; reflex -3.6 to -4.2 F). Stoppers that stopped by contact inhibition regrow only partly.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Contact-count brake (n_view) that releases when neighbours vanish (already in every grown lineage), plus correct fate at the wound edge (act daughters above sense cells).
candidates.positive_control: A GRN hand body that regrows: handbuilt.router_genome or column_genome with its n_view-gated division, wounded at T/2 and compared with its unwounded twin (paired fork by replay, t_open = kill_t). Hand program bodies cannot serve.
candidates.measurement: Regrown fraction = (n_end - (n_base - kills)) / kills; F over [kill_t, T] against the twin; time to recover the capture rate; births after kill_t from the fate log; p_die and apoptosis use.
candidates.engineering: Pure config today in kernel and reference (verified in exp1/exp2). JS port 0.5 day. Variants 0.5-1 day each.
candidates.risks: A uniform random kill is salt-and-pepper, not a lesion. Selection may favour a bigger reserve over regrowth (size cost answers). The hotspot can be killed, which stops all clicks.

candidates.name: (g) two blob types distinguishable by local cues
candidates.capability: Discrimination (approach one kind, avoid the other); lateral computation such as center-surround.
candidates.world_change: Size, brightness, value, presence and own-timer: pure config today via b2_sigma, b2_amp, b2_value (< 0 = avoid), b2_p and b2_mode 1. Flicker cue: prototype keys fl_half0/1 and fl_low0/1, a square wave by fmod(floor((t - t0) / half), 2) with no libm call, so it is bitwise portable; it comes with the (b) bundle (about +0.5 day). Receptor channel (S = 2): an organism change (per-channel g_r knob, a trace input, so NIN and GENOME_SIZE change, decode and founders' prior), ABI 4, user approval, 3-5 person-days. Use size or flicker first. JS needs a b2 port first (about 1 day).
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Peak receptor rate is identical for both blobs, so a single sensor cannot tell size; the reflex clicks the decoy. A big decoy draws 52 clicks/life (-32.9 F).
candidates.minimal_circuit: Surround suppression: rim and ring-1 sense cells inhibit the centre click sensor (or each other) when many are co-active, which signals a big blob. For flicker: a temporal filter (coincidence across about 1 unit, or refractoriness).
candidates.positive_control: reflex@hollow3 with S to C inhibition on channel 1 (ROUTER_GRID S.emit1, C.w1 < 0), re-tuned in the big-decoy world. It must beat the re-tuned reflex by more than 3 SE, and lateral_off must remove the gain.
candidates.measurement: Decoy clicks against captures; lateral_off and per-direction lesion of the S to C inhibition; P.ccg lat inhibition.
candidates.engineering: Size/brightness: none (config). Flicker: part of the (b) bundle. Receptor channel: 3-5 days plus approval.
candidates.risks: Decoy worlds currently have no positive F reference, so a fixed normalisation is undefined until the control exists. Twin- or decoy-heavy families select 'be smaller'. CPU per life 1.5-2.8x.
candidates.evidence_or_result: exp1: decoy_big dF reflex -32.87±0.42, router -24.29, s4 -24.62, s5 -15.61, s7 -26.81; twin_big_pays reflex +18.06. exp4: decoy_same reflex -10.57; decoy_flickers -6.28; target_flickers -14.56.

candidates.name: (h) fast / straight / accelerating targets (prediction, interception)
candidates.capability: Prediction and leading a moving target; delay-line motion detection.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Pursuit fails once v_t approaches the dot's speed. At v_t 0.4 the reflex (+0.67) only ties the motionless 2-cell clicker (+0.61) and s5 is negative, so chasing no longer pays.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Direction-selective delay lines (sense cell A to B with delta and a lateral relay, Reichardt-like coincidence) driving the motor on the side the target is heading to.
candidates.positive_control: A hand interceptor: role body with lateral delay relays (delta knob, channel-1 relay) feeding leading-side motors. It must beat both the re-tuned reflex and the clicker at v_t 0.3-0.4 (straight or head_mode crossing) by at least 3 SE. Without it, a fast world just selects sit-and-click.
candidates.measurement: Captures; lead angle of pulls relative to target bearing and velocity (probe tuning align against heading); chains with lateral hops; lateral_off.
candidates.engineering: Config today for v_t/tau_turn. Epoch phases via (b). Acceleration and head_mode 0.5-1 day each.
candidates.risks: No headroom is shown yet; the clicker matches the reflex in fast worlds.

findings.claim: Six task variations were measured with hand-built positive controls against the best reflex on fresh paired lives. Three have real headroom: the routing family (V1), wounds (V2) and POOL-SPECK (V5). Three fail: width decoys (V3), motor flip (V4) and the cued flip (V6).
findings.evidence: Seeds fresh_seeds(n, 40,500,000 + 5000*block). Confirmations used 1,024 lives on blocks 12, 13 and 17, which no tuner saw. 'Best reflex' is the max over the re-tuned and frozen reflex@hollow3/ring3 ON THE EVALUATION LIVES, which favours the reflex. Pass rule: lead > 3 paired SE, and lesioning the mechanism removes at least the lead. Results: V1 +3.25±0.12 (z 26.6), lateral_off -10.85 (3.3x the lead). V2 +0.51±0.10 (z 5.3) over the family and +1.09±0.13 (z 8.4) in wounded lives; division_off at the wound -2.11 (1.9x the lead). V5 +5.83±0.10 (z 58), lateral_off -11.43 (2.0x). V3 -0.05±0.12. V4: the honest switch loses -3.02. V6: the switch never latched, -0.94. Summary: headroom/results_summary.json.

findings.claim: V1 ROUTE family (existing keys only) passes strongly. The router re-tuned on the family keeps its lead in every member except fast targets. Its lead is carried by multi-hop lateral relay.
findings.evidence: Family: base 25%; d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25 alone 12.5%, or plus one of lam_s 4, sigma 0.4 + lam_s 4, v_t 0.05, lam_bg 0.2, v_t 0.3 (12.5% each). Router lead per member (confirm, 1,024 lives): base +2.03±0.20, fast +4.30, fast+bright +6.26, speck0.4 +3.83, slow +4.93, noisy +2.46, quick (v_t 0.3) +0.16±0.21 (not significant). lateral_off removes 5.3-17.6 F per member. P.chains (3 reference lives each, every trace checked bitwise against the kernel): 49% (base) and 56.5% (fast+bright) of the router's rim-motor receptor chains start in another column and are relayed; the reflex has 0%. Latency by hop count: 1.0/2.02/3.08/4.19 at d0 1 and 0.50/1.01/1.53/1.99 at d0 0.5.

findings.claim: Re-tuning the reflex on a family can overfit the tuning lives. Leads must be taken against the best of the re-tuned and frozen reflexes on fresh lives.
findings.evidence: V1: the reflex re-tuned on 192 hill lives reached hill F +8.15, but on fresh lives scored 7.83 against the frozen reflex's 7.98 (-0.15±0.07). The same happened in V4, V5 and V6: the frozen reflex was best in V6, and the re-tuned one in V2, V3 and V5.

findings.claim: V2 WOUND family (existing panel keys kill_t / kill_frac) passes. The regenerating GRN router (capabilities regen7, copied unchanged) beats the best reflex only in wounded lives, and its advantage is regrowth.
findings.evidence: Family: 50% unwounded; the rest kill_t ~U[256, 768] with kill_frac 0.25 or 0.5 (25% each). Confirm, 1,024 lives. regen7 vs re-tuned reflex@hollow3: unwounded -0.06±0.14; k25 +1.40±0.19; k50 +0.78±0.18; wounded +1.09±0.13. regen7 minus its non-regenerating twin: wounded +1.79±0.11, unwounded +0.05. division_off forked at kill_t: -2.71 (k25), -1.50 (k50), -2.11 over wounded lives. Size is regulated: n_end 125 after the wound against 123 unwounded (twin 80, reflex 35). Caveat: the larger non-regenerating program router@ring4 still has the best family F (8.11 against regen7's 7.17) and gains +0.69 in wounded lives through redundancy. The GRN router base is weak, and that costs the regen body more than regrowth gains.

findings.claim: V5 POOL-SPECK (sigma 0.4, lam_s 4, d0 0.5, d_min 0.25; existing keys) passes. It is the only world where the evolved bodies beat the best reflex, so it offers a continuous path from pooling to routing.
findings.evidence: Confirm, 1,024 lives. Best reflex (re-tuned hollow3) 4.92. Router re-tuned +10.75, lead +5.83±0.10, lateral_off -11.43±0.10. s5 +1.16±0.08 (whole life) and +1.55±0.10 post-256, with lateral share 0.86. s7 +0.32±0.07, post-256 +0.67, lateral share 0.94. This matches the niche map (+5.61 / +1.28).

findings.claim: Check against 'variation just selects smaller reflex bodies'. Routing, wound and pool worlds do not make the smaller reflex win. Decoy and flip lives shrink the size penalty sharply, so they push toward 'be smaller'.
findings.evidence: reflex@hollow2 minus best reflex: V1 -2.34±0.10; V2 unwounded -3.17, wounded -1.44; V5 -0.42±0.07 (pool narrows the gap but evolved large bodies win there). V3: base -2.77 against decoy lives -0.39. V6: normal lives -3.46 against cue/flip lives +0.48 (the smaller body loses less when everything fails). Evolved s5/s7: behind in V1 (-0.89 / -1.77 post-256), V2 (about -1.1 wounded, -1.8 unwounded), V3 (-2.19 / -1.40 in decoy lives), V4 and V6. Ahead only in V5.

findings.claim: V3 WIDTH-DECOY fails. No local centre-surround body beats the re-tuned reflex. Given the choice, the tuner switches the pursuit veto off. Hand pursuit vetoes make decoy capture worse.
findings.evidence: Family: 50% base, 50% decoy lives (b2_amp 1, b2_sigma 1.2 against target sigma 0.6, b2_mode 0, b2_p 0.5, b2_value -10). 512 lives. Re-tuned reflex: base 8.39, decoy lives 3.05 (10.7 captures, 42 decoy clicks), so the upper bound is about 5.3 F per decoy life. cs@hollow3 (rim S-S ch1 inhibition plus ring-1 J -> C click veto), tuned with 200 evaluations: lead -0.05±0.12 (decoy lives -0.15). The tuner chose S.emit1 0 and a weak veto (J.g_r 0.25, J.b 0.625, C.w1 -0.5); lateral_off changes F by +0.10±0.08. Hand settings in the all-decoy world (128 lives, x_decoy_explore.log): rim inhibition S.w1 -0.25 to -1.5 kept captures at 4.2-5.3 (reflex 5.5) and raised decoy clicks from 81 to 103-118. Click vetoes cut decoy clicks but cost base captures (21.3 -> 10.3-17.7). The router loses in decoy lives (-0.97±0.14) because its relays spread decoy evidence.

findings.claim: V4 FLIP (scratch t_flip) fails as a positive control, though the bound is large. A hidden-plane latch and broadcast circuit does switch pathways when triggered. The bottleneck is the local trigger: no single cell can tell the contexts apart within its time constants.
findings.evidence: Family: 50% unflipped, 25% flipped from t0, 25% flipped at U[256, 768]; 512 lives. Oracle switch (annulus-norm before the flip, annulus-flip after): +2.10 per family life (+5.73 flipped-from-t0, +2.67 mid-life). annulus-flip in flipped-from-t0 lives: +5.61±0.17 against the reflex, but -10.28 in unflipped lives. Forced-latch switch body (W fires at once): +3.25±0.14 in flipped-from-t0 lives. hidden_off from t0 removes it (forced coincC +1.89 -> -1.96, dF -3.85), so the hidden planes carry the context. Honest watchdog (W reset by hotspot spikes): family -3.02±0.24. It latched in 90% of unflipped lives (median t 300) against 96% of flipped ones (median 188). With a coincidence centre it latched in every life (median 74). Why: with the tuned single-event centre, hotspot spikes are mostly background clicks (65/life unflipped against 43 flipped; max gap 63 against 88). With a coincidence centre, normal lives still have gaps up to 342 units, and flipped lives make their first click at a median of 230. Rim-motor bursts differ only 2x (251 against 122 per life). Separating the contexts needs about 100-300 units of integration, while program-mode cells top out at tau_m 16.

findings.claim: V6 FLIP-CUE across lives (flipped lives also have lam_bg 0.2 as a sensory cue) also fails. The hotspot-rate cue detector separates the contexts poorly. Under the cue's noise the inner pathway is weak, and the hidden circuit costs about 0.7 F per normal life.
findings.evidence: 512 lives. Oracle (annulus-norm in normal lives, annulus-flip in cue lives) +2.07±0.15 against the best reflex (frozen, 3.42). The screen picked W.w0 0.25, which never latches; that switch equals its no-trigger twin at -0.94±0.10 against the reflex (hidden cells -0.68 against annulus-norm in normal lives). f6_cue_diag.log: W.w0 0.25 with b 0.25 latched in 31% of normal and 100% of cue lives (median t 160), but cue-life F was only -1.32 against annulus-flip's +2.30. W.w0 0.375 latched in 88-100% of normal lives. The cause: the hotspot's t_ref of 4 caps its rate, so the cue raises hotspot spikes only about 1.7x.

findings.claim: Engineering: a 2-line scratch-kernel patch gives program bodies up to 16 fixed-row phenotypes. It is bitwise neutral, and it makes 6+-role hand bodies (latches, relays, detectors) cheap to build. The capabilities scratch kernel also has a latent bug.
findings.evidence: make_hkernel.py = capabilities make_xkernel.py plus: (1) fixed rows >= 5 are read from PROGRAM_SIZE + 23*(row-5); (2) b2 epochs run only when h_inc == 555. h0_neutral.log: the full ledger, except the repurposed columns 21-22, equals the repo kernel for reflex@hollow3, router@ring4 and s5 in base, b2 and kill worlds; a body moved to rows 5-9 equals the original; the fast and full builds agree. The bug: the original xkernel switched b2 epochs on whenever tau_R > 0 and tau_e > 0, and the World defaults are 6 and 0.5, so every b2 world run on it had blob-1 epochs. No groundwork script ran b2 worlds on that kernel, but a FLIP-CUE with b2 epochs built on it would have been affected. Neither the extended rows nor t_flip is in reference.py or lifesim.js; both are scratch only.

candidates.name: V1 ROUTE family (fast-conduction routing region, drawn per life)
candidates.capability: (1) routing / multi-hop relay
candidates.world_change: Existing keys only. A stratified draw per life: base SPECK 25%; d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25 alone 12.5%, or plus one of lam_s 4, sigma 0.4 + lam_s 4, v_t 0.05, lam_bg 0.2, v_t 0.3 (12.5% each). CRN: members keyed by life index with a fixed rng.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Interior act cells cannot pull, so while the target is over the interior a column reflex does not steer, and it reacts to lone background events. Fast hops let relayed interior evidence reach the rim motors while the target is still there.
candidates.minimal_circuit: router@ring4: interior coincidence sensors J emit on ch1 only, and rim sensors S listen (w1) and drive the rim motor above them. That is J -> S -> M, 1-2 lateral hops.
candidates.positive_control: router@ring4 re-tuned on the family (analysis.tune_knobs, ROUTER_GRID, 150 hill evaluations on 192 family lives; knobs in v1_route_tuned.json). The reflexes hollow3 and ring3 were re-tuned the same way, and the frozen reflexes were kept as references.
candidates.measurement: Confirm, 1,024 fresh lives: lead against the best reflex, per member; whole-life lateral_off fork (dF against the lead); P.chains on rim motors (rec_other_col and relayed share, latency by hops); s5/s7 post-256 lead and lateral share; reflex@hollow2 against hollow3.
candidates.engineering: None in kernel.c, reference.py or lifesim.js. A per-life member draw in evaluate.py (about 40-60 lines; the engineering study's fam_eval.py already works inside evolve_life).
candidates.risks: The fast-target member gives no lead to a family-tuned router (+0.16±0.21), while a world-tuned router leads +3.35 there (niche map). Members want different relay gains, so the family rewards a compromise. Evolved bodies still trail here (s5 -0.89, s7 -1.77 post-256) with lateral shares of 0.62/0.74, so selection may stay on the pooling path.
candidates.evidence_or_result: PASS. Best reflex: frozen reflex@hollow3 at 7.98. Router re-tuned 11.23; lead +3.25±0.12 (z 26.6); lateral_off -10.85±0.16 (3.3x the lead). Per member: base +2.03, fast +4.30, bright +6.26, speck0.4 +3.83, slow +4.93, noisy +2.46, quick +0.16. Chains: relayed 0.49 (base) and 0.565 (fast+bright) against reflex 0.00; latency 0.50/1.01/1.53/1.99 at d0 0.5. reflex@hollow2 -2.34±0.10.

candidates.name: V5 POOL-SPECK (small bright halo plus fast conduction)
candidates.capability: (1) routing, reached through lateral pooling that already pays
candidates.world_change: Existing keys: sigma 0.4, lam_s 4, d0 0.5, d_min 0.25 on catch_speck_l4. It can also be a member of the V1 family.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: A 0.4 halo covers about one sense cell, so per-column evidence is sparse. Pooling and relaying neighbour evidence to the rim is needed.
candidates.minimal_circuit: Step 1: s5-style cooperative sensors (weak lateral excitation). Step 2: the router's one-hop J -> S relay to the rim motors. Each step pays on its own.
candidates.positive_control: router@ring4 re-tuned in the world (150 hill evaluations). Evolved s5 and s7 unchanged.
candidates.measurement: Lead against the best reflex on 1,024 fresh lives; whole-life lateral_off on the router; post-256 lateral_off share for s5/s7; reflex@hollow2 against hollow3.
candidates.engineering: None (world keys). A config change for a SPECK run.
candidates.risks: Low F levels (best reflex 4.9, 13 captures per life). The size penalty of a small reflex shrinks (hollow2 only -0.42). Evolution may stop at pooling, which already beats the reflex. d0 0.5 re-baselines the gates.
candidates.evidence_or_result: PASS. Best reflex: re-tuned hollow3 at 4.92. Router re-tuned 10.75; lead +5.83±0.10 (z 58); lateral_off -11.43 (2.0x the lead). s5 +1.16±0.08 (post-256 +1.55, lateral share 0.86). s7 +0.32±0.07 (post-256 +0.67, share 0.94). Frozen router +2.73.

candidates.name: V2 WOUND family (cells lost mid-life)
candidates.capability: (6) regeneration / size regulation; gives division a job after development
candidates.world_change: Existing panel keys: 50% of lives unwounded; the rest kill_t ~U[256, 768] with kill_frac 0.25 or 0.5 (stratified). A per-life fork at kill_t is exact (replay).
candidates.why_reflex_fails: Program bodies never divide. Losing the hotspot (0,0,1) or the centre sensor ends clicking, and lost rim columns cut pursuit. The re-tuned reflex keeps 4.63 F in wounded lives against 8.68 unwounded.
candidates.minimal_circuit: A hole detector in mature, formerly interior sense cells (slow INNER memory, lineage-timer gate, maturity flag, FULL = all 7 contacts). The cell divides into the empty slot: up if its act cell died, else into the hole. The hotspot also accepts a ch1 (J-type) centre.
candidates.positive_control: capabilities regen7 (router_genome plus GATE/MAT/FULL/LOSS genes, K.w1 = 1), copied unchanged into v2_wound.py. Twin: router_genome without the regen genes. Reflexes re-tuned on the family (120 hill evaluations).
candidates.measurement: Lead against the best reflex per member; regen minus twin; a division_off fork at kill_t (whole-life F against the same-fork twin); n_end after the wound against unwounded; births after the wound.
candidates.engineering: None in kernel or reference. lifesim.js lacks KILL (port about 30 lines). Per-life draw in evaluate.py.
candidates.risks: A bigger redundant non-regenerating body (router@ring4) gains +0.69 in wounded lives and has the best family F, so the variation partly rewards size or redundancy. The GRN router base is weak (twin about -0.4 against the reflex), so regeneration gains are partly eaten by development cost. Evolved bodies do not use regrowth (s5/s7 division_off at the wound about 0).
candidates.evidence_or_result: PASS (narrow on the whole family, clear in wounded lives). Confirm, 1,024 lives. regen7 against the best reflex: family +0.51±0.10 (z 5.3), unwounded -0.06±0.14, k25 +1.40±0.19, k50 +0.78±0.18, wounded +1.09±0.13. Against its twin, wounded +1.79±0.11. division_off at the wound: -2.11±0.09 over wounded lives. n_end 125 after the wound (twin 80). The 512-life run (block 5) agreed: +0.44±0.13 / +0.88±0.18.

candidates.name: V3 WIDTH-DECOY family (same-peak wide decoy)
candidates.capability: (5) discrimination by spatial extent (centre-surround)
candidates.world_change: Existing b2 keys: 50% base lives, 50% decoy lives with b2_amp 1, b2_sigma 1.2 (target sigma 0.6), b2_mode 0, b2_p 0.5, b2_value -10, b2_rho 1.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: It pulls toward and clicks any glow. In decoy lives the re-tuned reflex falls from 8.39 to 3.05 F (10.7 captures, 42 decoy clicks).
candidates.minimal_circuit: Tried: rim lateral inhibition (S emits ch1, S.w1 < 0) for pursuit, plus ring-1 surround sensors J that veto the centre click (C.w1 < 0). The niche probably needs a two-hop surround or an avoid pathway: once the body sits on a wide blob its rim sees almost nothing, so a rim veto cannot pull it off.
candidates.positive_control: cs@hollow3 (decoy_body.py: centre, ring 1 J, ring 3 S; full act disk), tuned on the family with 200 hill evaluations from a veto-on start. Hand sweep in the all-decoy world as well. Not passing.
candidates.measurement: Captures and decoy clicks per life type; lead against the re-tuned reflex; lateral_off; knob knockouts S.w1 = 0 and C.w1 = 0.
candidates.engineering: None (b2 exists in kernel and reference). lifesim.js needs the b2 port (about 80-100 lines).
candidates.risks: Decoy lives shrink the size penalty (hollow2: -2.77 in base against -0.39 in decoy lives), so they select 'be smaller'. Fixed vetoes cost base captures. Routers lose more (-0.97).
candidates.evidence_or_result: FAIL. cs lead -0.05±0.12 (base +0.06, decoy -0.15). The tuner set S.emit1 0 and a weak click veto. lateral_off +0.10±0.08. Hand pursuit vetoes in the all-decoy world: captures 4.2-5.3 against the reflex's 5.5, and decoy clicks rose from 81 to 103-118. Click vetoes cut decoy clicks but lose 3.6-11 base captures. s5 in decoy lives -2.19.

candidates.name: V4 FLIP family (motor sign flips; uncued)
candidates.capability: (4) context switching / within-life adaptation, plus (2) persistence held in the hidden planes
candidates.world_change: Scratch kernel hkernel (t_flip in the drift_tau slot: strokes at t >= t0 + t_flip push instead of pull). Family: 50% unflipped, 25% flipped from t0, 25% flipped at U[256, 768]. Needs kernel.c, reference.py and lifesim.js work (about 5-10 lines each) plus a reserved key.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: After the flip every column pushes its target away: 0 captures when flipped from t0 (F -1.54).
candidates.minimal_circuit: An act-plane annulus with two pathways: outer motors for the normal law, inner-rim motors (faces into the empty ring 1) for the flipped law. A hidden-plane context circuit: watchdog W above the hotspot, a 2-cell latch L/L' at z = 3, and a relay sheet at z = 2 whose beats enable the inner motors (Min.w1 > 0) and silence the outer ones (Mout.w1 < 0).
candidates.positive_control: switch_body in flip_bodies.py (9 program rows via the scratch extended-row kernel). The forced-latch variant proves the hardware works; the honest watchdog variant is the local trigger. Not passing: the trigger fails.
candidates.measurement: F per member against the best reflex; oracle switch bound; latch time per context (raster of L); hidden_off fork from t0; no-trigger twin.
candidates.engineering: t_flip in all three engines. Extended program rows for hand controls are scratch only (a 2-line kernel patch; not needed for evolution).
candidates.risks: The contexts are separable only over about 100-300 units: successes are sparse, roughly one click per capture, and most clicks and rim bursts come from background events. Program cells (tau_m <= 16) cannot integrate that long. A GRN slow gene (lambda ~1/128 per tick, about 256 units) or a denser consequence signal is needed. Wrong-context switching is catastrophic (-10 F).
candidates.evidence_or_result: FAIL for the honest trigger; the latch hardware works. 512 lives. Oracle +2.10 per family life (+5.73 flipped from t0, +2.67 mid-life). Forced latch in flipped-from-t0 lives: +3.25±0.14 against the reflex (9.3 captures against annulus-flip's 11.7); hidden_off removes it (dF -3.85). Honest watchdog: family -3.02±0.24, latched in 90% of unflipped lives (median t 300) against 96% of flipped ones (median 188); with a coincidence centre it latched in all lives (median 74).

candidates.name: V6 FLIP-CUE across lives (flip signalled by 4x background)
candidates.capability: (4) cued context switching plus (2) a latched context in the hidden planes
candidates.world_change: Scratch t_flip plus the existing key lam_bg: 50% normal lives (lam_bg 0.05), 50% lives flipped from t0 with lam_bg 0.2. A mid-life cue would need an epoch feature.
candidates.why_reflex_fails: In cue lives it pushes targets away, and the cue doubles its misses (F -2.23).
candidates.minimal_circuit: The V4 latch and relay sheet, with W as a rate detector of hotspot spikes (W.w0 > 0, tau 16). A better detector would pool background events from many sensors without being fooled by a local target.
candidates.positive_control: switch_cue in v6_flipcue.py (W.w0 screened over 0.25-0.625 on 96 separate lives), plus a cue-only control world (cue without the flip). Not passing.
candidates.measurement: F per context against the best reflex; oracle; latch fraction and time per context; hidden_off and no-trigger twins; the cue-only control.
candidates.engineering: t_flip in all three engines (lam_bg exists).
candidates.risks: The hotspot's t_ref caps its rate, so the cue raises hotspot spikes only about 1.7x. Background noise also weakens the inner pathway (cue-life F -1.32 even when latched, against annulus-flip +2.30). The hidden circuit costs about 0.7 F in every normal life.
candidates.evidence_or_result: FAIL. Oracle +2.07±0.15 against the best reflex (frozen, 3.42). The screened switch (W.w0 0.25) never latched and equals its no-trigger twin (-0.94±0.10). Diagnostics: W.w0 0.25, b 0.25 latched in 31% of normal and 100% of cue lives; W.w0 0.375 latched in 88-100% of normal lives.

critiques.critic:
Constraints-purist verdict: only the worlds built from existing keys survive, and even those need changes before they can be used for selection: V5 POOL-SPECK, a reshaped V1 ROUTE family, and V2 WOUND. Every world that needs a new key (FLIP, FLIP-CUE, BLINK, epochs, payoff swap, AVOID, head_mode/acceleration) fails two ways. It has no passing positive control, and it exists only in a scratch kernel (the engineering bundle also has a Python mirror), so the rule kernel = reference = JS is not met.

Checks I ran myself, beyond reading the reports:
- **Evolved bodies in V1, per member** (from headroom/confirm_v1_F.npz): s5 and s7 trail the best reflex in 6 of 7 members (base -1.70/-1.90, fast+bright -3.43/-3.54). They lead only in fast+speck04 (+1.42±0.26 / +0.97±0.20), which is V5. The frozen, un-retuned router already gets +2.98 of the +3.25 family lead.
- **V2 against the strongest non-regenerating body** (confirm_v2_F.npz): regen7 minus the frozen program router@ring4 is -0.95±0.11 over the family and +0.40±0.14 in wounded lives (2.9 SE).
- The headroom report's 'redundancy' reading is wrong. The router loses 5.6 F to a wound against the reflex's 4.05. Its lead shrinks from +2.22 (unwounded) to +0.69 (wounded); it does not grow.
- **JS engine**: lifesim.js:552-553 throws for kill_t >= 0 and b2_amp > 0. It does read d0, d_min, sigma, lam_s, lam_bg, v_t and tau_turn, so V1 and V5 run in all three engines.
- **Scratch-kernel bug**: none of the capabilities scripts that used the scratch xkernel set any b2 key (checked with grep). So the b2-epoch bug (epochs on whenever tau_R > 0 and tau_e > 0) did not touch any reported b2 result. It does sit inside the proposed FLIP-CUE b2-epoch design.
- **Life length**: life_catch.yaml draws T per generation from {768, 1024, 1536}. Every headroom number used T = 1024, and kill_t ~U[256, 768] can land at the very end of a T = 768 life.
- **Already done**: N1 random tie-breaking is already in src/evolve.py (rank_desc, evolve.random_ties, RESULTS 2026-10-10).
- **Member id**: World.name is in _META, not in the world vector, so carrying the member id in the name does not perturb lives.

Constraint findings, most serious first.
1. **V1 varies d0 / d_min per life.** These are cell-side physics: the kernel reads them in cell handlers, and newborns learn their contacts at 2·d_min. So drawing them per life randomises the organism, not the task. The N5 gate (re-tuned router at least +3.0 over the re-tuned reflex, lateral_off removing at least 50%) is already met by the niche map: d0 0.5, fresh 1,024 lives, +4.52, share 0.71-0.92. Adopt d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25 once as the fixed base. That is a minor tweak to report (it re-baselines GS1-GS6), and the family then varies task keys only.
2. **V1 was chosen by the hand router's lead.** N6 says A2 must be judged against every computing reference, including evolved pooling bodies, 'so that worlds are not chosen to suit our own hand-built router'. V1 breaks this; V5 is the only world that passes it.
3. **Per-world scale constants taken from a reference body's F** (engineering (a), L1) weight the family toward that body's strengths. That is a designer constant. Raw mean F needs no constant, and it is what every headroom number used. Any scaling needs Q3 approval and a body-independent justification.
4. **Single-shot kill_t / kill_frac in selection.** These keys are robustness-panel perturbations (ABI 7.9). The user's pending Q5 asks about kill_rate, not about these. Most of the wound loss is the hard-coded tap site (0,0,1) or the centre sensor, so the regeneration job is largely 'regrow the designed identity' (Q6). No control uses apoptosis, so 'gives genome-driven death a job' is unsupported.
5. **Designed behaviour smuggled in through the world:**
   - FLIP-CUE pairs lam_bg x4 with the flip, a designer-chosen contingency that acts as a body-wide context channel delivered through every receptor.
   - The flicker cue's phase is anchored at t0 (fmod(floor((t - t0)/half), 2)), so every sensor gets a shared pacemaker.
   - head_mode ('targets pass near the body') exists only to make an imagined interceptor pay.
   - The V3 decoy price (-10) was set at the reflex's break-even, and the peaks were equalised to rule out single-cell answers.
   - AVOID's per-time sting cost inside b2_rho is a distance-threshold dense cost: the rejected distance shaping with the sign reversed.
6. **Schedules.** The POET/ACCEL 'regret-curated' loop with a band on the current champion is population-dependent, which is the dropped c_miss-ramp pattern. MVG's fixed-E switch is population-blind but is still a designer schedule over generations, so it needs approval.
7. **Payoff swap relabels ledger columns by state** (captures = rewarded clicks). The ledger identity holds, but the meaning of probe and analysis columns silently changes.
8. **Scratch kernels** reuse reserved or BELL-only slots (drift_tau for t_flip; kill_rate / wound_rate for blink; th_lo, tau_R, tau_e and h_inc gated by the magic values 555 / 777). Extended program rows are a tool for building controls. A control that passes only with them does not show GRN reachability; regen7 being a GRN genome is the right pattern.
9. **Literature caution.** Kashtan, Noor & Alon 2007 found that scoring many goals at once (the simultaneous multiobjective control) gave virtually no speedup. A per-life mixture (L1) is that design, so 'more task variation' through L1 alone has published evidence against it producing modular circuits. The temporal-switching form needs a schedule approval.

Items that need the user's approval:
- Q3 / decision 8: fitness over a family, plus any normalisation constants.
- Per-life d0 draws, if anyone still wants them; fixed N5 is only a report-to-user tweak.
- The wound variant: kill_t / kill_frac as a selection axis, distinct from Q5's kill_rate.
- Q4: epochs and every new world key (each with an ABI number and three-engine ports).
- Decision 3: the tap-cell consequence signal, for uncued flip or swap.
- X1 face weights, or a chiral morphogen, for an interceptor.
- A second receptor channel (S = 2) for discrimination.
- AVOID's per-time sting cost.
- A cue contingency (FLIP-CUE).
- An MVG generation schedule.
- Any population-dependent curation.

N2 (resume) and probe readouts need no approval. Scratch prototypes need none either, as long as they stay in scratch.

reviews.name: V5 POOL-SPECK (sigma 0.4, lam_s 4, d0 0.5, d_min 0.25), also nichemap POOL-SPECK and the V1 'fast+speck04' member
reviews.notes:
Cleanest candidate under the constraints:
- Existing keys only, and every one of them is read by kernel.c, reference.py and lifesim.js.
- Raw F; one continuous life; confirmed on 1,024 fresh lives on the repo kernel.
- The only world where evolved bodies beat the best reflex (s5 +1.16±0.08, s7 +0.32±0.07), so its headroom is not defined by our hand router. That satisfies N6.
- The router's +5.83 lead with lateral_off -11.43 shows room for routing above pooling.

Conditions:
- Adopt d0 0.5 as the fixed base under N5 (report it to the user; rerun GS1-GS6), not as a world-specific trick.
- Check A1 here (clicker and S0 champion above the lone cell).
- Watch the shrunken size penalty (hollow2 only -0.42), a 'be smaller' risk.
- Measure at T 768 and 1536 too, because T is drawn per generation.

reviews.name: V1 ROUTE family (and capabilities ROUTE-FN, nichemap ROUTE-FAST)
reviews.notes:
Passes on the numbers: +3.25±0.12, lateral_off 3.3x the lead, hop-quantised relay chains. It breaks the rules in two ways.

(1) d0 / d_min is a family axis. Base 25% of lives run at d0 1, the rest at 0.5. These are cell-side physics: they set conduction delay and the 2·d_min contact-learning window. Drawing them per life randomises the organism, and N5 never approved that. N5's gate is already met (niche map, fresh lives: +4.52 re-tuned, share 0.71-0.92). So fix d0 0.5 / d_min 0.25 for every life (a reported minor tweak) and vary task keys only: lam_s, sigma, v_t, lam_bg, t_resp.

(2) Members were picked by the hand router's lead, against N6. Computed from confirm_v1_F.npz: s5 and s7 trail the reflex in 6 of 7 members (base -1.70/-1.90; fast+bright -3.43/-3.54). They lead only in speck04 (+1.42/+0.97). So the family rewards our designed relay, not the path evolution is on (niche-map Spearman -0.34). Weight the speck04 / V5 region more, and keep members such as 'quick' that do not favour the router. Do not prune on the router's numbers.

Also:
- Use raw mean F, or get approval for any scale constant (Q3).
- Draw members with a hash keyed on run, generation and life, not numpy default_rng.
- Rerun the confirmation with d0 fixed, and at T 768 and 1536.
- ROUTE-FAST ('bright' + slow) is a single tilted world: keep it only as a family member.

Needs approval under Q3 / decision 8.

reviews.name: Task family per life inside the routing/pooling region (nichemap) and engineering (a) family harness
reviews.notes:
Closest to the constraints. d0 is fixed at 0.5 and task keys are drawn per life. The harness keeps CRN (engineering exp6: recheck alignment, identical genomes give identical F). World.name is a _META field and is not in the kernel vector (verified), so carrying the member id there is safe.

Modify three things.
(a) Normalisation:
- Drop 'scale = best positive control's F'. It weights the family toward that hand body, a hidden designer weighting.
- Continuous draws make 'one constant per world' ill-defined anyway.
- Default to raw mean F. Only an additive offset cancels under CRN, and the scale is exactly the designer choice.
(b) Exclusion rules must follow N6. Judge each member against every computing reference, evolved bodies included, not 'where the router wins'.
(c) Life length:
- Validate kill_t against the T actually drawn, or express it as a fraction of T.
- The configured T_choices are {768, 1024, 1536}.

Keep base at 25-50% as the A1 stepping stone. Using it for selection needs Q3 / decision 8. The code itself, behind a config flag that is off by default, needs no approval. Literature caveat: Kashtan 2007's simultaneous-mixture control gave virtually no speedup, so do not expect this alone to produce modular circuits.

reviews.name: V2 WOUND family (and capabilities WOUND, nichemap WOUND-512, literature WOUND lives, engineering (f))
reviews.notes:
Constraint-clean where it matters:
- kill_t / kill_frac exist in kernel and reference.
- The kill is hash-keyed per uid (CRN holds within a body).
- One life, and the fork at kill_t is exact by replay.
- regen7 is a local GRN genome, confirmed on the repo kernel with fresh lives.
- Size is regulated (n_end 125 against 123).

Problems:
(1) Three-engine exactness: lifesim.js throws for kill_t >= 0 (line 552, verified), so a JS KILL port is required before selection use.
(2) These are robustness-panel keys (ABI 7.9). Q5 asked about kill_rate. Single-shot kills as a selection axis are a different design and need their own approval (decision 8).
(3) T: kill_t ~U[256, 768] was measured only at T 1024. With the per-generation T of 768, a kill can land at the end of life. Use u·T.
(4) The pass compares against the reflex only. I computed regen7 against the frozen non-regenerating router@ring4: wounded +0.40±0.14 (2.9 SE), family -0.95±0.11. The headroom report's 'router gains through redundancy' is a misreading: its lead shrinks from +2.22 to +0.69. Pre-register the margin over the strongest non-regenerating body. The regrowth-specific evidence is regen minus its GRN twin (+1.79) and division_off (-2.11).
(5) Most of the loss is the hard-coded tap site, or the centre that feeds it (lives losing K 0.0 late captures; losing C 0.07), so the job is mostly 'regrow the designed identity' (Q6). Report rim regrowth separately.
(6) No control uses apoptosis, so drop the claim that this 'gives genome-driven death a job' until a p_die knockout says otherwise.

reviews.name: V3 WIDTH-DECOY family (and literature WIDTH-DECOY)
reviews.notes:
Fails: centre-surround -0.05±0.12, and the tuner switched the veto off.

Constraint concerns even if it had passed:
- The world was parameterised around the pre-imagined circuit. Peaks were equalised specifically to rule out single-cell solutions, and the price (b2_value -10) was set at the reflex's break-even, which tunes the world to one reference body.
- Decoy lives cut the size penalty (hollow2 -2.77 in base against -0.39 in decoy lives), which selects 'be smaller'.
- lifesim.js has no b2 (it throws), so it breaks three-engine exactness until ported.

The 'hotspot latch on a blob that survived a click' add-on would use b2_mode 0 persistence. That is ABI-defined world physics, so legitimate, but untested.

reviews.name: V4 FLIP (motor sign flip, uncued) and capabilities FLIP, engineering (d)
reviews.notes:
Drop for now; revisit only behind a new gate.
- The honest local trigger fails (family -3.02±0.24; it latched in 90% of unflipped lives).
- The oracle and forced-latch numbers are bounds, not positive controls.

Constraint issues:
- t_flip exists only in scratch kernels (capabilities xkernel; headroom hkernel, in the reserved v3 drift_tau slot). There is no reference.py mirror and no JS. The engineering ep_motor bundle has a bitwise xref mirror but no JS.
- The switch control uses scratch extended program rows (9 rows), so even a pass would not show GRN reachability.
- A one-way latch handles one flip only.

The diagnosis is useful: separating the contexts needs 100-300 units of integration. GRN slow genes (lambda ~1/128 per tick) could do that.

Before asking for decision 3 (the tap-cell consequence bit), test whether the consequence the world already shows is enough. After a capture the target is re-placed, so its halo vanishes from under the body; a successful click is therefore locally visible through the receptors.

Any adoption needs a new key in all three engines, an ABI number and Q4 / decision 8.

reviews.name: V6 FLIP-CUE across lives (and capabilities FLIP-CUE b2-epoch variant)
reviews.notes:
Fails: the switch never latches, -0.94±0.10.

Constraint objections beyond the failure:
- The cue (lam_bg x4 if and only if flipped) is a designer-chosen contingency that exists so a pre-imagined cue-gated switch can work.
- A uniform background change reaches every receptor equally, so it acts as a body-wide context broadcast built into the world. That is the global channel the locality rule forbids inside the body.
- The cue itself costs misses, so it is not neutral.
- The capabilities variant's b2 epochs (e_on / e_off) inherit the xkernel bug, which ran epochs whenever tau_R > 0 and tau_e > 0. hkernel patches this with a magic h_inc == 555 gate in a BELL slot; neither may be ported as is.

If cues come back, they should be properties of objects (for example a feature of blob 1), not world-wide rate shifts, and they need Q4 approval.

reviews.name: BLINK / FLASH (capabilities), BLINK / catch-blind (literature), engineering (c) blink
reviews.notes:
No positive control passes:
- the best memory variants gain +0.10 to +0.27;
- naive holds lose 1.4 to 6.8 F;
- it matches L4's prior occlusion null (+0.05).

Engineering:
- The capabilities version exists only in a scratch kernel (blink in the reserved kill_rate / wound_rate slots, dark_amp gated by a magic h_inc value 777), with no reference mirror and no JS.
- The engineering ep_amp0 = 0 version has a bitwise xref mirror but no JS, and it needs an ABI number and Q4.

L4's gate (beat the re-tuned reflex by at least 3 SE) is unmet, so it must not launch.

Keep the measurement ideas: hidden_off during gaps, I(E:M|S).

reviews.name: LEAD (capabilities), FAST-TARGET (nichemap), engineering (h) fast/straight/accelerating targets
reviews.notes:
Drop as a separate world.
- No interceptor exists.
- The clicker matches the reflex at v_t 0.4 (exp8).
- The router's lead at v0.3 / tau 200 is -0.33.

v_t and tau_turn can stay as natural axes inside the family, at <= 0.2 mostly.

Constraint flags:
- head_mode ('targets pass near the body') and acceleration are world rules invented to create interception headroom. That is designed behaviour smuggled in through the world.
- A 'chiral morphogen pattern' would hard-code handedness.
- Face weights are X1 and need approval.
- 'Score F(tau200) - F(tau5)' must be a readout only, never fitness.
- The +1.20 hold-twin result used an unpaired SE on what should be CRN-paired lives. Redo it paired.

reviews.name: POISON (capabilities), nichemap b2-decoy negative result, engineering (g) two blob types
reviews.notes:
No headroom: the veto loses (-0.44 to -0.75) and decoys select click discipline.

Constraint issues:
- lifesim.js has no b2, so these worlds are not exact across the three engines.
- A second receptor channel (S = 2) is an organism change (ABI 4, a new genome size) and needs the user's approval.
- The flicker cue in (g) uses a square wave with its phase anchored at t0, a shared pacemaker for every sensor. If it is ever used, the phase should be hash-random per placement.
- The blob-type table that would retire the b2 keys is L2 work and needs approval.

Discrimination should come back only after a passing control, preferably one that is context-gated.

reviews.name: AVOID (stinging blob)
reviews.notes:
Fails several constraints:
- The proposed per-time cost while within b2_rho of the stinger is a dense distance-threshold cost computed by the accountant. It is the rejected distance shaping with the sign reversed, and it would breed 'stay far from everything' or immobility.
- An event-based sting (charged on entry or on click, like c_miss) would be the constraint-compatible form.
- It needs new keys, an ABI bump, a JS b2 port, and a discrimination step that has not been shown to pay.
- The stinger's amp and sigma would be picked to suit the annulus inner pathway, so the world would be designed around a planned circuit.
- No positive control: annulus-flip in the normal world gets 0 captures.

Needs approval in any form.

reviews.name: EPOCHS with visible consequences (literature) and engineering (b) two-state telegraph
reviews.notes:
Keep the engineering prototype in scratch as ready infrastructure; do not merge it. Its good points:
- the start state is drawn stationary, so there is no 'A first' time cue;
- lambda_max is the maximum over states (verified in kernel_x.diff);
- only accountant-side keys switch, and prices never switch;
- it is bitwise equal to xref in 90/90 lives.

Gaps:
- No JS port. The JS needs b2 and KILL first.
- No passing adaptive control, so L2's gate (beat both the fixed body and the reflex across a mixture) is unmet: V4 and V6 fail.

Fix three things before it is ever used:
(1) Flicker phase anchored at t0: randomise it per placement.
(2) ep_swap relabels 'captures' to mean rewarded clicks by state: use explicit per-state columns.
(3) ep_bg is a world-wide cue channel, the same objection as V6.

Needs Q4, an ABI number and new reserved-key entries.

reviews.name: Engineering (e) which blob pays switches mid-life
reviews.notes:
Without a cue or the pending consequence signal (decision 3), value is invisible to cells: behaviour is identical at prices 0-400 under CRN. The cue variants are designer contingencies.

It also relabels ledger semantics by state, and it uses b2, which lifesim.js lacks.

Revisit only if the receptor-visible consequence (a capture re-places the target; in b2_mode 0 a decoy click leaves the decoy in place) is shown to be enough, and then with explicit per-state ledger columns.

reviews.name: MVG-SWAP (Kashtan modularly varying goals over generations)
reviews.notes:
As proposed (halo width that pays flips every E generations), it has no headroom: V3 shows no discrimination control, and the phase asymmetry (reflex +19.2 against +8.6) forces per-phase designer normalisation.

A fixed-E switch is population-blind, which avoids the specific flaw of the dropped c_miss ramp. It is still a designer schedule over generations and changes the fitness function in time, so it needs explicit approval.

It is the only variation scheme with direct published support for modular circuits; the simultaneous mixture got virtually no speedup. So if pursued, re-target it onto members that already pass and share the relay subproblem (for example V5 against fast+noisy, no new keys). Pre-register the re-adaptation time and the speedup against the L1 mixture.

reviews.name: Regret-curated family (PAIRED / POET minimal criterion / ACCEL edits)
reviews.notes:
The online form breaks the constraints:
- A band on the current champion's score, with re-curation every 100 generations, is a population-dependent schedule, the dropped c_miss-ramp pattern.
- Regret computed from our hand bodies picks worlds that suit them, which N6 forbids.
- ACCEL edits automate designer world-tuning.

Acceptable form: one offline pass, effectively the niche map already done. A2 is judged against every computing reference (evolved bodies included), and the family is then frozen in config and population-blind. An ANNECS-style count can stay as a readout. Any online loop needs approval.

reviews.name: N2 checkpoint/resume with determinism pinning
reviews.notes:
Pure harness, no organism or world rule, and no approval needed (POST_PILOT_CALLS N2). Family and epoch draws are hash-keyed, so they resume for free.

Add the tie generator's state, since random_ties is now in the repo (seed + 7,919,001). The byte-equality test must strip wall-time fields.

reviews.name: N1 random tie-breaking
reviews.notes:
Already in the repo: src/evolve.py rank_desc, evolve.random_ties default on, RESULTS 2026-10-10. The scratch evolve_x prototype is superseded; nothing further is needed.

As the prototype showed, it does not by itself rescue the 1-cell plateaus. It is neutral on runs without exact ties.

critiques.critic:
I re-ran the load-bearing checks on fresh lives: fresh_seeds(n, seed0 = 40,700,000 + 5000*block), blocks 0-4. Scripts, logs and JSON are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jgon-project-ml-cell-dev/aefb0c66-3af5-49c4-936c-154d6434706c/scratchpad/taskvar/critic/ (c1_v1, c2_path + c2b_steps, c3_wound, c4_grn, c5_grn_tuned). I ran 4-6 threads and was the only cell-dev job on the machine.

1. V1 replicates, but it is a change of regime, not variety. On 1,024 lives the family-tuned router leads the best reflex by +3.08±0.12 (headroom found +3.25), and lateral_off costs -10.72. The frozen base-tuned router does as well on the family: +3.03 (F 11.02 against 11.07). So the family asks for no new or more general circuit. It just pays more for the same router, because conduction is faster.
   - Per member: base +1.83, fast +3.46, bright +5.26, speck04 +3.67, slow +4.50, noisy +2.99, quick +0.55 (z 2.5).
   - Re-tuning the reflex overfits again: re-tuned hollow3 scores 7.86 on fresh lives, the frozen one 7.98.

2. Most of the routing value is one lateral hop. Setting J.w1 = 0 cuts J-to-J listening but keeps the 1-hop J->S relay.
   - It costs -1.30±0.10, which is 42% of the lead.
   - By member: base -0.45 (25%), speck04 -2.02 (55%), quick -1.66 (more than that member's whole lead).
   - Caveat: J.w1 also feeds J's own coincidence detection, so this is an upper bound on the value of 2 or more hops.

3. The lead depends on the price of a cell. The router has 66 more cells than the reflex.
   - c_live x2: +1.76±0.12.
   - c_live x3: +0.44±0.12 (reflex not re-tuned).
   - c_msg x4: no effect (+3.05).
   - So keep c_live where it is.

4. Largest confound: development cost.
   - Every headroom number except V2 compares program-mode bodies that are fully built at t0. Evolved bodies have to grow.
   - The GRN-grown router (hb.router_genome, same knobs, 123 cells) pays 1.8-3.2 F for development. Against the program reflex:
     - base: +0.06±0.14 (the program router gets +2.26)
     - fast (d0 0.5): +0.55 to +0.60 (program +3.4 to +3.8)
     - pool (V5 knobs): +3.83±0.14 (program +5.68)
   - Against s5: the grown router leads by +2.85±0.14 in pool and +1.87 in fast. With frozen base knobs in pool it trails s5 by -0.37.
   - So the headroom evolution can actually reach is about 0.6 F in V1-like worlds and about 3-4 F in V5.

5. Growth path (the GS3 grid with the hollow3 reflex's knobs plus routing knobs, 768 lives):
   - Base: the widest path dips -0.23±0.09 (z -2.5), and the first step, filling the interior, is -0.10.
   - Fast: no step falls. The smallest is +0.04±0.11, the first step is +1.01±0.12 (z 8.4), and the end is +3.83.
   - Pool: the first two steps are +1.12 and +1.74 (means). F peaks at ring 3 + 4 columns (+3.73 over the reflex) and then falls as columns are added.
   - Fast conduction turns the base plateau-with-valley into a ramp. In pool, filling the interior with relaying sensors pays almost +3 F at once.

6. V2 WOUND replicates (512 lives).
   - Regen minus twin: +1.86±0.17 (z 10.9) in wounded lives, -0.03 in unwounded ones.
   - Regen minus best reflex: +0.96±0.19 wounded, -0.05 unwounded.
   - The 2-cell hotspot lottery is not what drives it. The wound took K or C in 57% of wounded lives, and the gain is the same with or without that loss: +1.82±0.23 against +1.90±0.25.
   - But on the whole family, the bigger non-regenerating program router still wins: +2.24 in unwounded lives, and only +0.23±0.15 in wounded ones (headroom found +0.69).

7. Noise is not a concern for V1, V2 or V5 (z 5-40). It is a concern for selection: the steps along the path are +0.04 to +1.0 F, against a paired per-life SD of about 3-4 F and 3+4 lives per generation.

Which variations are decisive and cheap:
- **POOL-SPECK (V5).** Existing keys, and the only world where all of these hold:
  - a grown router has large headroom over both the reflex and s5;
  - the path from the reflex is uphill;
  - evolved pooling bodies already beat the reflex, so the route from pooling to routing can be watched.
- **Fast conduction (d0 0.5)** comes next. Its gradient is clean, but the grown-body headroom is small (+0.6).
- **WOUND** is cheap and passes, but it tests development and regrowth, not circuitry.
- Discrimination (V3), flip (V4/V6), blink and lead have no passing positive control. The flip and blink worlds would also need new world features in all three engines.

Proposed first experiment. Existing keys only, after N1 (random tie-breaking) and the per-life draw. All arms on the same harness:
- (B) base SPECK as the control;
- (P) POOL fixed;
- (PV) the same world drawn per life as a mixture, for example pool, fast+bright, base and 50% wounded lives;
- optionally (PM) temporal switching every E = 30 generations, Kashtan's arm. This is the only design that separates "variety" from "a better world".

Endpoints, pre-registered against GRN-level bars, not only the program reflex:
- the best beats s5's F by more than 3 SE on 1,024 fresh lives;
- the P.chains relayed share (and the share with 2 or more lateral hops) rises above s5's 0.22-0.27;
- lateral_off from t 256 removes at least 50% of the lead;
- reflex@hollow2 is checked for size selection.

A cheaper pre-test, a few CPU-hours: the distribution of fitness effects (DFE) of random s5 mutants on paired lives in base against pool. It shows whether pool gives a gradient where evolution actually sits.

reviews.name: V5 POOL-SPECK (small bright halo plus fast conduction)
reviews.notes:
Main arm of the first experiment. It is decisive, cheap (existing keys only) and replicated:
- The program router leads by +5.68±0.14 (c5) and +5.83 (headroom).
- The GRN-grown router with V5 knobs is +3.83±0.14 over the reflex and +2.85±0.14 over s5. This is the only world where routing headroom survives development cost.
- The path from hollow3 is uphill, and the first fill step is worth about +2.9.

Endpoint: report it against s5, not only against the reflex, because s5 is already +0.98 to +1.16 over the reflex here. Watch two things:
- the low capture count (about 13 per life);
- a small size penalty (hollow2 -0.42).
The nichemap's 'POOL-SPECK world' is the same candidate, and its '+4.3 headroom above pooling' is program-mode; the grown figure is +2.85.

reviews.name: V1 ROUTE family (fast-conduction routing region, drawn per life)
reviews.notes:
The program lead replicates: +3.08±0.12, with lateral_off -10.72. But:
- The family-tuned router equals the frozen base router (+3.03). The family asks for no new circuit; it is a stronger-gradient regime, not variety.
- The GRN-grown router gains only about +0.6 in fast and +0.06 in base.
- The 'quick' member adds nothing (+0.55, z 2.5), and the base member gives grown bodies nothing.
- About 42% of the lead needs J-J interaction (the J.w1 = 0 lesion); the rest is a single hop.

Change: keep d0 0.5 (with d_min 0.25) as a world constant (re-baseline the gates, N5), and use pool or fast+bright as the members. Run it as a mixture arm only to test whether variety itself does anything. It covers ROUTE-FN, ROUTE-FAST and the nichemap's per-life routing family.

reviews.name: V2 WOUND family (cells lost mid-life)
reviews.notes:
Replicated on fresh lives:
- Regen minus twin: +1.86±0.17 in wounded lives.
- Regen minus reflex: +0.96±0.19 wounded, -0.05 unwounded.
- The gain is not just regrowing the hotspot: it is the same whether the twin lost K or C (+1.82) or kept both (+1.90).

Caveats:
- On the family, the bigger non-regenerating program router wins (+2.24 unwounded, +0.23 wounded), so the reward specific to regrowth is about +0.9 per family life, and only for a GRN body.
- s5 and s7 do not regrow in any way that pays.
- It tests development (regrowth), not circuitry.

Cheap: existing keys; only lifesim.js lacks KILL. Add it as 50% of lives in one arm (pool x wound) rather than as a routing vehicle. It covers WOUND, WOUND-512, (f) and the literature's 'WOUND lives as modular variant'.

reviews.name: N1 random tie-breaking (harness, do first)
reviews.notes: A prerequisite: about 26 lines, neutral when no fitness values tie, and it restores turnover. Without it, tied-parent runs (seeded starts) freeze. It is not decisive for any capability on its own.

reviews.name: N2 checkpoint/resume with determinism pinning (harness, do first)
reviews.notes: Useful for runs of 500+ generations and for spot-rented machines, but not needed for a first 300-500-generation experiment on local cores. Do it in parallel; it should not block.

reviews.name: (a) task family drawn per life, with fixed per-world normalisation
reviews.notes:
The harness container, about 110 lines; the prototype fam_eval.py already runs. Rules:
- Set each member's scale from a GRN-grown positive control's F, not a program body's. Program bodies overstate headroom by 1.8-3.2 F.
- Stratify slots so each 3+4-life generation covers the members.
- Do not mix in members where the reflex wins (twin food, near placement, wide halo, decoys).

reviews.name: Regret-curated family (PAIRED / POET minimal criterion / ACCEL edits over existing keys)
reviews.notes: The principle is right: admit a member only where a computing control beats the re-tuned reflex. But regret must be measured with GRN-grown controls (c4/c5: development wipes out most of V1's lead) and against max(frozen, re-tuned) reflex on fresh lives. Today it would admit only pool, fast/bright and wound, which is a short list. Re-curating at checkpoints is a schedule, so freeze the list after the niche map.

reviews.name: MVG-SWAP: which halo type pays flips every E generations (Kashtan modularly varying goals)
reviews.notes: Temporal switching against a simultaneous mixture is the only design here that tests 'variety' as distinct from 'a better world', so keep the arm structure: fixed, mixture, switching. But the width swap depends on a discrimination module that has no positive control (V3 fails). Until one exists, alternate goals that each pass, for example pool and pool+wound, and first measure the generations needed to recover after a switch.

reviews.name: V3 WIDTH-DECOY family (same-peak wide decoy)
POISON: a same-peak broad poison blob (two blob types)
reviews.notes: Same evidence as V3: the veto loses -0.44 to -0.75 against the re-tuned reflex, and lateral_off changes nothing. A dim poison is solved by one cell's threshold, and a broad poison that is always present is a cliff. Not a first experiment.

reviews.name: Discrimination with b2 decoys (negative result for the existing keys)
reviews.notes: Agree it is negative: the re-tuned reflex wins by clicking less, routers spread decoy evidence, and decoy-wide fails A1.

reviews.name: (g) two blob types distinguishable by local cues
reviews.notes: Size and brightness are config today, but no control passes (see V3). Flicker needs the epoch bundle. A receptor channel needs ABI 4 and approval. Park it until a body beats the re-tuned reflex.

reviews.name: AVOID: a stinging blob (the ladder's 'withdraw' rung in this world)
reviews.notes: Needs new accountant work and the b2 port to JS. Its discrimination step has not been shown to pay, and the local annulus route would make it a morphology task. Later.

reviews.name: V4 FLIP family (motor sign flips; uncued)
reviews.notes: The bound is real (oracle +2.10 per family life), and the forced latch shows the hidden-plane hardware works (hidden_off dF -3.85). The honest trigger fails, though: program cells cannot integrate the 100-300 units needed, and wrong-context switching costs about -10 F. Next step, before any change to the three engines: a GRN slow-gene watchdog (lambda about 1/128) as a positive control in the scratch kernel. Also needs the annulus morphology. Not a first experiment. Covers FLIP (and FLIP-CUE) and (d).

reviews.name: V6 FLIP-CUE across lives (flip signalled by 4x background)
reviews.notes: The cue detector separates contexts poorly: the hotspot's t_ref caps its rate, so the cue raises hotspot spikes only about 1.7x. The cue also doubles misses and costs about 0.7 F in every normal life. Drop the background-rate cue; any cued flip needs a cue that does not damage the reflex.

reviews.name: (b) within-life epochs: two-state telegraph of accountant-side world keys
reviews.notes: Good engineering (bitwise kernel = reference, neutral when off), but nothing that would run inside an epoch has a passing positive control yet (flip, blink, swap). Shelve kernel_x until a GRN switch control passes. If built, add per-state ledger columns and keep lambda_max fixed per life. Covers the literature's EPOCHS candidate.

reviews.name: (e) which blob pays switches mid-life
reviews.notes: No cell can observe value: prices re-bill identical lives under CRN. It is unlearnable without a cue or the pending local consequence signal (a user decision).

reviews.name: BLINK (and FLASH): the target goes dark
reviews.notes: Four memory controls fail A2: naive holds lose up to 6.8 F, and the best variant gains +0.27±0.10. This echoes the earlier occlusion result (+0.05, matched by a single slow cell). Needs a body-wide 'nobody sees it' veto that nobody has built, plus work in all three engines. Covers (c) and the literature's BLINK / catch-blind.

reviews.name: LEAD: fast targets on straight runs (the ladder's 'jump' rung in this world)
reviews.notes: No interceptor control exists. The hold twin gains only against its own weak GRN-router base, which is about -2 against the reflex at v 0.3. At v_t 0.4 the static clicker ties the reflex (exp8), so fast worlds select 'sit and click'. Covers FAST-TARGET and (h).

reviews.name: FLIP (and FLIP-CUE): the motor sign flips mid-life
reviews.notes: Same as V4 and V6: the oracle bound is real but no honest switcher passes. Build the GRN slow-gene trigger control first; the flipped-from-t0 context across lives is the easier first rung.

critiques.missing:
Gaps in the groundwork, roughly in order of importance:

1. **Grown controls for every headroom claim.**
   - Every claim except V2 compares program-mode bodies built at t0. The GRN-grown router loses 1.8-3.2 F to development: +0.06 in base, about +0.6 in fast, +3.83 in pool (c4/c5).
   - Each world's headroom, member scale and pass rule should be restated with a GRN control, and with s5 as a second bar.

2. **No test separates variety from a better world.**
   - The family-tuned router equals the base-tuned one, so V1 says nothing about variety.
   - Needed: arms with a fixed world, a per-life mixture and temporal switching (Kashtan's MVG), run on the same harness, with re-adaptation time measured.

3. **Evolvability where evolution actually sits.**
   - A cheap DFE test: about 256 random s5 mutants on paired lives in base and in pool. It gives the fraction of beneficial mutants, and whether those mutants raise lateral reliance or relayed share.
   - The GS3-style path (c2) is for program bodies only.

4. **Selection noise budget.**
   - Steps along the path are +0.04 to +1.0 F, against a paired SD of about 3-4 F per life and 3+4 lives per generation.
   - Estimate the probability of fixing the first fill step in pool, or use 2x-4x lives per generation there.

5. **Routing endpoints for evolved bodies.**
   - Report the P.chains hop distribution: the share with 2 or more lateral hops, not only relayed of at least 1.
   - J.w1 = 0 shows about 58% of the hand router's lead is one hop.
   - Fix the bar now: relayed share above s5's 0.22-0.27, and a lead over s5 of more than 3 SE.

6. **Price sensitivity.**
   - The routing lead nearly vanishes at c_live x3 (+0.44). Record that c_live is a load-bearing constant and freeze it before any run.

7. **Gate re-baseline (N5)** if d0 0.5 becomes the base. Also measure CPU per life in pool: router about 87-91 ms against 34 ms for the reflex.

8. **Overfitting.** The tuner's hill F overstates fresh F by 0.3-0.5 for both reflex and router, replicated here (re-tuned hollow3 7.86 against frozen 7.98). Always take max(frozen, re-tuned) on unseen lives.

9. **Playground ports.** lifesim.js lacks KILL and b2, so the wound arm will not show in the playground until KILL is ported (about 30 lines).

10. **Discrimination and flip need positive controls, not more worlds.** The next work there is a GRN slow-gene context trigger, and a 2-hop surround through a hidden relay, both in the scratch kernel.
